-Do not brush your hair when wet! Use a wide tooth comb and start and ends and work your way up.
-Do not brush or comb your hair in the shower! Do it before.
-Gently work shampoo into the top of your head and squeeze the foam down (don't pile on your head and/or rub. It breaks hairs.)
-Gently apply conditioner to the ends of your hair. Take excess and gently work up hair by squeezing. (Again, Don't pile and/or rub!)

Epilation is a more effective hair removal method for women than shaving or waxing. Epilators gently remove hair at the root, rather than at the surface like shaving, and can remove much shorter hair than waxing so you don't have to wait until hair becomes visible to remove it. After epilation, legs stay smooth for up to four weeks and hair grows back at different rates, meaning you will typically have less hair to remove each time you epilate. What is the benefit of epilation versus using a traditional razor, cream, or foam? Unlike shaving, cream, or foam - which only cut or dissolve hair at the skin surface - epilators remove hair at the root. Because it takes a while for the hair to grow back to the skin surface, your skin will stay smooth for up to four weeks. As the hair grows back from the root, the tip of the hair will not be blunt, but instead look thinner and finer. As a result, you'll no longer have the feeling of coarse stubble. What is the benefit of epilation versus waxing (Agda or Halawa)? Wax does remove hair from the root just like epilators. However, when it comes to removing shortest hair, wax performs quite poorly. As wax basically sticks on the hair to remove it, hair needs to be a certain length for this process to take place. Therefore, there is a hair-growth waiting period for those who use wax. With epilators, there is no such waiting and therefore no need to cover legs up. Using wax is also a hassle. The preparation process (for self-made wax, Adga, or Halawa) is long, messy, and tiresome. What's even worse, using wax (Agda or Halawa) is a more painful process compared to epilators. Does epilation hurt? Most women trying epilation for the first time find the process much less painful than they had anticipated. As hair is removed at the root, however, there might be some discomfort. In the beginning, the pulling sensation is stronger, but this subsides as your skin adjusts to the process. Over time, after successive epilations, there is also less hair to be removed. Studies show that epilating more frequently can reduce pain significantly. Silk-épil Xpressive also features three ways to help women minimize discomfort - Olay pre-epilation wipes prepare the skin for epilation, a new massage system stimulates the skin before epilation and helps reduce the pain, and a beginner cap helps new users get used to epilation. How long does my hair have to be for epilation? Silk-épil can remove hair that is 0.5-mm in length. This hair length occurs after approximately two days of not shaving. Will my hair grow back after epilation? Yes. However, the hairs will grow back more tapered and fine than they do from shaving. Hair that is removed with a razor is cut at skin level, so that the edge grows back blunt and coarse, causing razor stubble. Does hair grow back thicker and stronger after epilation? No, dermatologists have confirmed that epilation has no negative impact on the thickness of regrowing hair. In addition, because hairs are removed at the root, the hairs that do grow back have softer, narrower tips than hairs removed with a razor, so they feel softer and finer to the touch. The reason why this question arises every now and then is that hair removal is more frequent (and also more in focus) in summer. And this is also the time when hair growth itself changes. Due to the higher ambient temperatures the blood circulation is better, leading to a better supply of nutrition to hair roots so that hair growth in general is stronger.

Epilation is a more effective hair removal method for women than shaving or waxing. Epilators gently remove hair at the root, rather than at the surface like shaving, and can remove much shorter hair than waxing so you don't have to wait until hair becomes visible to remove it. After epilation, legs stay smooth for up to four weeks and hair grows back at different rates, meaning you will typically have less hair to remove each time you epilate. What is the benefit of epilation versus using a traditional razor, cream, or foam? Unlike shaving, cream, or foam - which only cut or dissolve hair at the skin surface - epilators remove hair at the root. Because it takes a while for the hair to grow back to the skin surface, your skin will stay smooth for up to four weeks. As the hair grows back from the root, the tip of the hair will not be blunt, but instead look thinner and finer. As a result, you'll no longer have the feeling of coarse stubble. What is the benefit of epilation versus waxing (Agda or Halawa)? Wax does remove hair from the root just like epilators. However, when it comes to removing shortest hair, wax performs quite poorly. As wax basically sticks on the hair to remove it, hair needs to be a certain length for this process to take place. Therefore, there is a hair-growth waiting period for those who use wax. With epilators, there is no such waiting and therefore no need to cover legs up. Using wax is also a hassle. The preparation process (for self-made wax, Adga, or Halawa) is long, messy, and tiresome. What's even worse, using wax (Agda or Halawa) is a more painful process compared to epilators. Does epilation hurt? Most women trying epilation for the first time find the process much less painful than they had anticipated. As hair is removed at the root, however, there might be some discomfort. In the beginning, the pulling sensation is stronger, but this subsides as your skin adjusts to the process. Over time, after successive epilations, there is also less hair to be removed. Studies show that epilating more frequently can reduce pain significantly. Silk-épil Xpressive also features three ways to help women minimize discomfort - Olay pre-epilation wipes prepare the skin for epilation, a new massage system stimulates the skin before epilation and helps reduce the pain, and a beginner cap helps new users get used to epilation. How long does my hair have to be for epilation? Silk-épil can remove hair that is 0.5-mm in length. This hair length occurs after approximately two days of not shaving. Will my hair grow back after epilation? Yes. However, the hairs will grow back more tapered and fine than they do from shaving. Hair that is removed with a razor is cut at skin level, so that the edge grows back blunt and coarse, causing razor stubble. Does hair grow back thicker and stronger after epilation? No, dermatologists have confirmed that epilation has no negative impact on the thickness of regrowing hair. In addition, because hairs are removed at the root, the hairs that do grow back have softer, narrower tips than hairs removed with a razor, so they feel softer and finer to the touch. The reason why this question arises every now and then is that hair removal is more frequent (and also more in focus) in summer. And this is also the time when hair growth itself changes. Not sure I would use this before going to bed though, my irritated skin definitely wasn't helping me fall asleep. People with very sensitive skin might want to look for something a little softer though.

Epilation is a more effective hair removal method for women than shaving or waxing. Epilators gently remove hair at the root, rather than at the surface like shaving, and can remove much shorter hair than waxing so you don't have to wait until hair becomes visible to remove it. After epilation, legs stay smooth for up to four weeks and hair grows back at different rates, meaning you will typically have less hair to remove each time you epilate. What is the benefit of epilation versus using a traditional razor, cream, or foam? Unlike shaving, cream, or foam - which only cut or dissolve hair at the skin surface - epilators remove hair at the root. Because it takes a while for the hair to grow back to the skin surface, your skin will stay smooth for up to four weeks. As the hair grows back from the root, the tip of the hair will not be blunt, but instead look thinner and finer. As a result, you'll no longer have the feeling of coarse stubble. What is the benefit of epilation versus waxing (Agda or Halawa)? Wax does remove hair from the root just like epilators. However, when it comes to removing shortest hair, wax performs quite poorly. As wax basically sticks on the hair to remove it, hair needs to be a certain length for this process to take place. Therefore, there is a hair-growth waiting period for those who use wax. With epilators, there is no such waiting and therefore no need to cover legs up. Using wax is also a hassle. The preparation process (for self-made wax, Adga, or Halawa) is long, messy, and tiresome. What's even worse, using wax (Agda or Halawa) is a more painful process compared to epilators. Does epilation hurt? Most women trying epilation for the first time find the process much less painful than they had anticipated. As hair is removed at the root, however, there might be some discomfort. In the beginning, the pulling sensation is stronger, but this subsides as your skin adjusts to the process. Over time, after successive epilations, there is also less hair to be removed. Studies show that epilating more frequently can reduce pain significantly. Silk-épil Xpressive also features three ways to help women minimize discomfort - Olay pre-epilation wipes prepare the skin for epilation, a new massage system stimulates the skin before epilation and helps reduce the pain, and a beginner cap helps new users get used to epilation. How long does my hair have to be for epilation? Silk-épil can remove hair that is 0.5-mm in length. This hair length occurs after approximately two days of not shaving. Will my hair grow back after epilation? Yes. However, the hairs will grow back more tapered and fine than they do from shaving. Hair that is removed with a razor is cut at skin level, so that the edge grows back blunt and coarse, causing razor stubble. Does hair grow back thicker and stronger after epilation? No, dermatologists have confirmed that epilation has no negative impact on the thickness of regrowing hair. In addition, because hairs are removed at the root, the hairs that do grow back have softer, narrower tips than hairs removed with a razor, so they feel softer and finer to the touch. The reason why this question arises every now and then is that hair removal is more frequent (and also more in focus) in summer. And this is also the time when hair growth itself changes. Due to the higher ambient temperatures the blood circulation is better, leading to a better supply of nutrition to hair roots so that hair growth in general is stronger.

Epilation is a more effective hair removal method for women than shaving or waxing. Epilators gently remove hair at the root, rather than at the surface like shaving, and can remove much shorter hair than waxing so you don't have to wait until hair becomes visible to remove it. After epilation, legs stay smooth for up to four weeks and hair grows back at different rates, meaning you will typically have less hair to remove each time you epilate. What is the benefit of epilation versus using a traditional razor, cream, or foam? Unlike shaving, cream, or foam - which only cut or dissolve hair at the skin surface - epilators remove hair at the root. Because it takes a while for the hair to grow back to the skin surface, your skin will stay smooth for up to four weeks. As the hair grows back from the root, the tip of the hair will not be blunt, but instead look thinner and finer. As a result, you'll no longer have the feeling of coarse stubble. What is the benefit of epilation versus waxing (Agda or Halawa)? Wax does remove hair from the root just like epilators. However, when it comes to removing shortest hair, wax performs quite poorly. As wax basically sticks on the hair to remove it, hair needs to be a certain length for this process to take place. Therefore, there is a hair-growth waiting period for those who use wax. With epilators, there is no such waiting and therefore no need to cover legs up. Using wax is also a hassle. The preparation process (for self-made wax, Adga, or Halawa) is long, messy, and tiresome. What's even worse, using wax (Agda or Halawa) is a more painful process compared to epilators. Does epilation hurt? Most women trying epilation for the first time find the process much less painful than they had anticipated. As hair is removed at the root, however, there might be some discomfort. In the beginning, the pulling sensation is stronger, but this subsides as your skin adjusts to the process. Over time, after successive epilations, there is also less hair to be removed. Studies show that epilating more frequently can reduce pain significantly. Silk-épil Xpressive also features three ways to help women minimize discomfort - Olay pre-epilation wipes prepare the skin for epilation, a new massage system stimulates the skin before epilation and helps reduce the pain, and a beginner cap helps new users get used to epilation. How long does my hair have to be for epilation? Silk-épil can remove hair that is 0.5-mm in length. This hair length occurs after approximately two days of not shaving. Will my hair grow back after epilation? Yes. However, the hairs will grow back more tapered and fine than they do from shaving. Hair that is removed with a razor is cut at skin level, so that the edge grows back blunt and coarse, causing razor stubble. Does hair grow back thicker and stronger after epilation? No, dermatologists have confirmed that epilation has no negative impact on the thickness of regrowing hair. In addition, because hairs are removed at the root, the hairs that do grow back have softer, narrower tips than hairs removed with a razor, so they feel softer and finer to the touch. The reason why this question arises every now and then is that hair removal is more frequent (and also more in focus) in summer. And this is also the time when hair growth itself changes. Due to the higher ambient temperatures the blood circulation is better, leading to a better supply of nutrition to hair roots so that hair growth in general is stronger.

review_title: Pretty sure it's just breaking the fine hairs off.
review_text: Being new to epilators I bought one and was underwhelmed, so I thought I'd try a few more and see if I could get any improvement. Enter the Braun Silk Epi, which is very highly rated so I thought I'd give it a try. At first I thought it was amazing, less pain than the first one I tried, but I noticed the fine hairs weren't actually being plucked, they were just shorter. Great, that's not what I'm going for here. Not to mention the fact that there's only the epilator head, and the brush head. There aren't even any guards to make the epilator head smaller if I wanted to pluck less hairs at once, even thought the pictures CLEARLY show that there are guards for this epilator. I went over the same sections over and over again, and frequently nothing seemed to happen. I adjusted the pressure I was using, the speed, everything. I'm pretty sure this is just breaking hairs off as opposed to actually doing anything. I also couldn't find any of the hairs that it was supposedly plucking. With my other epilator I would frequently stop and clean it out because the roots were getting stuck to the guard because hair roots are sticky (for lack of a better word), with this one there was never any evidence of plucked hairs sticking, which leads me to believe it was only ever breaking the hair off as opposed to pulling it out by the root. The brush is nice, ergo the second star, but if you want the brush you might as well just pick up a separate brush and a different epilator. Oh, and forget about trying to epilate your arm pits, I tried every direction and went over the areas over, and over to little effect. I finally went back over the areas with my old epilator.

review_text:
Like all too many organic soaps, this example ends up being a bit too subtle and bland in scent and power to justify its price point. I love vetiver but even with a generous dollop on the loofah, I get only the faintest scent of that fragrance here. The hemp / vetiver combo smells pleasant in a mild sort of way, but this is not what I expected at the price point and given the product name. If I wanted "fragrance free", I'd buy it!

Besides the really mild non-especially vetiverish scent, NH IH&V body wash also needs a lot of soap to generate any lather, and even needs a lot just to get through a whole body wash. Lather may or may not be to your liking, but having to reload the loofah halfway through your shower is no one's idea of fun. At the rate of product usage, I would be amazed if this 13 oz bottle lasts me for more than 2-3 weeks.

Ultimately, even if you want to stay organic, there are better choices with more prominent scents and better product consumption rates. EOs Cedar & Mint for Men works well enough and can even be used as a shampoo and shave cream for the undemanding. My personal favorite semi-organic products are from Every Man Jack. Their cedar and sandalwood (two separate types there) body wash have great smells and give adequate lather and cleaning duration with roughly half the product needed to get similar effects from NH IH&V wash. (I call Every Man Jack semi-organic as I haven't bothered to assess all the ingredients on their label, but they have no parabens or SLS derivatives, so they pass my personal screening standard.) Both of these product lines are much cheaper than Nubian Heritage.

For vetiver lovers who want that scent in their bath ritual, Provence Sante makes a good vetiver beauty bar soap, and also a rather expensive vetiver body wash. which I have not tried due to its high cost. I have tried the beauty bar, and though not cheap, it does indeed give the user a noticeable vetiver smell when applied, which is always a good thing when buying a vetiver named product!

review_text:
I've tried at least a dozen shave soaps, maybe two dozen. MWF is my go-to, standard. I leave it in a shave bowl in a drawer. I rinse my brush and then swirl the dripping wet brush on top of the soap. In about 20 seconds, you have phenomenal lather. Wet and repeat for more water if needed. Lather around your face further as needed. I often do this, then take a shower and repeat the lathering when I get out of the shower, and then shave.

I have found a few artisan soaps that lather as good, but none better. Those artisan soaps often come in a variety of delightful fragrances, but I don't care that much about fragrance. MWF doesn't have much of any fragrance. In fact after having wet it and let it dry a few dozen times, there is no discernible scent of any kind. If you like the smell of MWF (or any other shave soap), keep it in a covered container between uses. I'd suggest for those who like fragrance in their shave soap to just put MWF in a covered container and sprinkle in a little of their favorite cologne a few times and keep it covered and you'll have a $40 artisanal shave soap!

I like the ingredients. It's tallow based which I prefer. There's lanolin in it which I like. Although it's not a glycerin based soap, there is a little glycerin in the ingredients - it doesn't seem to be a large amount, so if you really like glycerin, get some vegetable glycerin on Amazon and sprinkle it on top of the soap or add it to your pre-shave. It doesn't have shea butter in it, so I sometimes keep an open puck of shea butter shave soap in a shave dish next to MWF and occasionally reach down with my brush and lather from both.

I've seen some reviews that say that it doesn't lather all that well in "hard" water. We have moderately hard water in my city and I've never had trouble at all.

Finally, it's cheap! I lather before showering; after showering, and usually a second time while shaving, and my brush is full of lather when I finish and my single puck will last for maybe 300 shaves?? so maybe 4 cents a shave??

Epilation is a more effective hair removal method for women than shaving or waxing. Epilators gently remove hair at the root, rather than at the surface like shaving, and can remove much shorter hair than waxing so you don't have to wait until hair becomes visible to remove it. After epilation, legs stay smooth for up to four weeks and hair grows back at different rates, meaning you will typically have less hair to remove each time you epilate. What is the benefit of epilation versus using a traditional razor, cream, or foam? Unlike shaving, cream, or foam - which only cut or dissolve hair at the skin surface - epilators remove hair at the root. Because it takes a while for the hair to grow back to the skin surface, your skin will stay smooth for up to four weeks. As the hair grows back from the root, the tip of the hair will not be blunt, but instead look thinner and finer. As a result, you'll no longer have the feeling of coarse stubble. What is the benefit of epilation versus waxing (Agda or Halawa)? Wax does remove hair from the root just like epilators. However, when it comes to removing shortest hair, wax performs quite poorly. As wax basically sticks on the hair to remove it, hair needs to be a certain length for this process to take place. Therefore, there is a hair-growth waiting period for those who use wax. With epilators, there is no such waiting and therefore no need to cover legs up. Using wax is also a hassle. The preparation process (for self-made wax, Adga, or Halawa) is long, messy, and tiresome. What's even worse, using wax (Agda or Halawa) is a more painful process compared to epilators. Does epilation hurt? Most women trying epilation for the first time find the process much less painful than they had anticipated. As hair is removed at the root, however, there might be some discomfort. In the beginning, the pulling sensation is stronger, but this subsides as your skin adjusts to the process. Over time, after successive epilations, there is also less hair to be removed. Studies show that epilating more frequently can reduce pain significantly. Silk-épil Xpressive also features three ways to help women minimize discomfort - Olay pre-epilation wipes prepare the skin for epilation, a new massage system stimulates the skin before epilation and helps reduce the pain, and a beginner cap helps new users get used to epilation. How long does my hair have to be for epilation? Silk-épil can remove hair that is 0.5-mm in length. This hair length occurs after approximately two days of not shaving. Will my hair grow back after epilation? Yes. However, the hairs will grow back more tapered and fine than they do from shaving. Hair that is removed with a razor is cut at skin level, so that the edge grows back blunt and coarse, causing razor stubble. Does hair grow back thicker and stronger after epilation? No, dermatologists have confirmed that epilation has no negative impact on the thickness of regrowing hair. In addition, because hairs are removed at the root, the hairs that do grow back have softer, narrower tips than hairs removed with a razor, so they feel softer and finer to the touch. The reason why this question arises every now and then is that hair removal is more frequent (and also more in focus) in summer. And this is also the time when hair growth itself changes. Due to the higher ambient temperatures the blood circulation is better, leading to a better supply of nutrition to hair roots so that hair growth in general is stronger.

review_text:
After hearing many times of "the fat" I decided to buy my own puck of Mitchell's and see what the fuss was about. It turned out to be a really great soap though not my favorite.

Lather:
Doesn't bloom into a full lather avalanche like TOBS does for me but isn't too thin either. Certainly adequate.

Face Protection:
On the slick side, good blade glide. Just for face protection alone this is a great product.

Cost:
A little on the high side. Razorock has similar soaps available for a third less. I'm not sure that they preform to exactly the same level but since I own some I will be putting this to the test. Not super extravagant though.

Scent:
This is where Mitchell's really loses me. I like strong scents with my shave. TOBS Mr. Taylor is great for a classic yet clean scent that sticks with you. Mitchell's smells like a bar of Ivory Soap. Clean for sure, but nothing to get excited about.

Overall:
I wish I could give Mitchell's 4.5 stars. It will give you a great shave. The price isn't that bad and the lack of strong scent may actually be preferable to some people. If you haven't tried it I suggest giving it a go.

description_text: What is jojoba oil? Jojoba (pronounced ho-HO-ba) oil is a botanical extract of the seed of the jojoba tree (Simmondsia chinenis). Technically it is not actually an oil, but rather what is called a wax ester. Why do we care? Because out of all of the compounds in nature, this wax ester is the most similar to human skin oil (sebum). It is theorized that applying jojoba to the skin can "trick" the skin into thinking it is producing enough oil, thus balancing oil production. The bottom line for acne-prone people is that jojoba oil is non-comedogenic so you can use it without fear. Benefits of jojoba oil Provides all day moisturization – jojoba oil doesn't evaporate like water based moisturizers can. It is theorized, but not yet proven, that because jojoba oil is so similar to human skin oil, it can "trick" the skin into thinking it has produced enough oil and thus balance oil production. Very stable – jojoba oil does not become rancid or lose antioxidants even after long periods of storage. Spreads well and absorbs well. The organic variety is free of pesticides, GMOs, and is sustainably farmed. Massage oil – Jojoba oil is perhaps the best massage oil on earth. A little goes a long way and for people with body acne is a welcome non-comedogenic option. Note: The skin irritation which sometimes comes with massage may still promote breakouts. review_text:
I purchased the base, color, and top coat from this company to give it a try. The label says it lasts 60% longer with the new formula. It doesn't say longer than what. Thankfully, I picked it up at a local store and was able to get a refund the same week.

The base coat goes on a little tacky, which isn't a bad thing. The brush is nice enough and the constancy of the polish is easy to work with. I didn't find it dried very quickly but I applied while watching movie so it didn't bother me. After adding the top coat, I had four coats on total. It was extremely shiny and gave my nail a nice feeling of thickness.

If it had stayed that way even for 3 days I would have been happy but the first chips (and I do mean chips along the sides, not tip wear) started about 36 hrs. in and by 48 hrs. I had chips on multiple fingers. I hadn't done anything but basic housework and shopping. No gardening, scrubbing laundry, scouring dishes, or anything harsh on my hands.

If you're someone who doesn't have a problem with polish staying on then this would probably be great for you. I have yet to find a base, polish, and top that actually stays put longer than two days so I'm still on the hunt. I do properly prepare my nails so it isn't an application issue. This brand is inexpensive, has pretty colors, and went on almost flawlessly. If I wanted to have a beautiful set of shiny nails for a wedding the next day, I would use it. I just wouldn't plan on needing the polish on longer than 24 hrs.

I do a lot of nail art that includes stamping, sponging and a bunch of other really messy designs. My problem is that when I do all of those things the polish gets all over my skin making clean up take a bit longer than I like. So I needed to find something that could help with that problem. In comes this liquid latex!

I ordered one in the hopes that it would help with keeping the skin around my nails clean while I'm doing those messy manicures. I cleaned out an empty nail polish bottle and filled it up with this liquid latex. Then I used the brush from the nail polish bottle to apply the liquid latex to the skin around my nails. I gave it a few minutes to dry then did my manicure. Once done with the manicure I used a little nail polish remover on a brush to make sure none of the latex was attached to the polish on my nail (don't want to ruin the manicure by pulling the polish on my nail off with the latex). Then, using tweezers, I pulled the latex off of each finger. For the most part it came off easily leaving clean up much easier with less to clean.

This was a lifesaver! I am very pleased with this liquid latex. The only thing I don't like about it is the smell, it's almost a fishy smell. It is very strong at first when applying. Once dried the smell does dissipate for the most part so it doesn't bother me that much.

review_title: Works well, but detailed instructions would have been helpful...
review_text:
For me, this little nail drill works very well. It's touted as being good for beginners, but I was really nervous about using it for the first time, because it came with absolutely no instructions. Yikes! I'd cut my nails down to nubbins, and have been wearing falsies, so I figured it was a great way to get some practice.

There are a few notes on the product listing about how to insert and remove the drill bits, so with that being all I had to go on, I just went for it.

As I had no clue as to which bits were for what job, I had to wing it. I tried two. The first I tried wasn't quite coarse enough, so I went with the larger, barrel-shaped bit, which worked well for what I wanted. I'd basically put on some stiletto tips, and managed to jab every family member at least once. I didn't want to completely remove them, but I wanted to take them down a bit and round out the tips. Once I changed the bit this drill did a great job.

It got a little warm, but didn't get too hot, and it didn't overheat and stop on me. In my photo is what they looked like right after I was done. I did go over the edges briefly with an emery board for the couple of rough spots left, simply because I'm not yet quite adept enough to get the perfect shaping I want, but practice is key.

It's for the same reason that I haven't yet tried the drill on my natural nails. I will, though, once I get a little more know-how under my belt. So, in summary, I like it, and it seems to be beginner-friendly, but I wish there were detailed information available on its use.

review_title: Nice Facial Cleaning Brush Offers Four Diverse Brush Heads but Only One Speed Option
review_text:
I'm very interested in trying new beauty products to pamper myself, and I have some dry skin on my face that I'm always struggling to keep in check, so it sounded appealing to give this waterproof facial brush cleaning system a try to compare and contrast to other similar products I own.

This skin cleansing kit comes with one waterproof and cordless rotating machine, one facial brush, one large body brush, one serum and moisturizer applicator sponge, and one pumice stone. This machine requires four AA batteries to run, which aren't included.

The brushes feel pleasant to the touch, and I liked that four different attachment heads were included. They are soft, but have just enough pressure to them to feel like they will exfoliate dirt, oil, and dead skin well. The set-up for this cleaning system is simple and straightforward, but I found it quite difficult to open the battery compartment on the end of the handle.

Once the batteries were inserted successfully and the battery compartment was snapped back into place, all that I needed to do was to pick a brush head and push it in to the attachment point. Then you can turn the unit on or off by pressing one of two buttons on the blue section of the brush. In my experience with the brushes, they didn't rotate evenly, and the brushes wobbled as they rotated. I'm not sure if this is an intended feature or not, but I'm suspecting it simply means the platforms for the brushes aren't quite even.

I'm glad that this cleaning system is waterproof, but I'll admit I was a bit underwhelmed that it only has one speed, and that that speed is rather slow. I still feel like I will get some good use out of it, but I would have liked if there were more speed options, because for attachments like the pumice stone, you really need a slightly faster speed for it to perform really well.

That said, I was generally pleased with the accessories offered in the kit, but would have liked if they included a small storage or travel bag of some kind.

Overall, I like this waterproof electric facial brush, and would recommend it if you're considering adding one to your own health and beauty routine. Just keep in mind it has only one slow speed, and that you will need to provide your own storage bag and batteries.

I am a longtime Amazon Prime customer who writes reviews in my free time. I was appreciative to be given an opportunity to test and review this waterproof facial brush cleaning brush complimentary for my honest and unbiased review. My first impression when I got this in the mail was, "Oh, that's a lot smaller than I imagined." And then, I open the bottle, and it is not even filled up to the top. It looks like it's already been used for a week. I attached a photo of how it looks after me only using it twice on my face and hands. That is why this product gets 4 stars instead of 5. For $25, I do not feel that you're getting your money's worth.

With that being said, Korean skin care is always amazing. This lotion in particular smells like roses, but it's not overpowering. It's also light enough where it absorbed into my skin, which I am happy about, because I want to be able to put this on in the morning and put makeup over top of it.

It does not make my skin look shiny. It's not tacky or sticky. It leaves my skin feeling very, very soft and luminous, which does make me look very youthful and pretty. Overall, I think this product does what it claims to do. It's a great skin care product, and I will use this every day, but it will probably only last me about one month. I am in my 20's, and I do not have any major skin problems or wrinkles. I am not the best case study for a before-and-after, but I do like this a lot more than many other lotions I have tried.

review_title: Gives that mascara a boost and conditions lashes too
review_text: I have never tried a lash primer and never really knew it existed until I saw this. Because I am getting older and we lose that wonderful thick lash look we have we are younger i thought it would be great to use to condition my lashes and keep them healthier and maybe keep from losing some. I didn't expect it to be white but it does make it easier to see when you apply it. I found it easier to apply by brushing across my lashing instead of brushing base to tip. I even used the very end of the brush so swipe across hard to get areas. I curled my lashes as usual, then applied the primer. I tried mascara immediately and also tried waiting for the primer to dry. It worked best for me after it dried. When I applied while the primer was wet it made my curled lashes droop and I couldn't tell I had curled them. But when I waited just a few minutes, because it does dry quickly, then applied I was very happy with the results. I would never apply , then curl for fear of pulling out lashes that might stick to the curler. I also use the product to condition my lashes while I sleep. I put on before going to bed each night. I think your lashes are just like your hair, they need care and conditioning to keep looking beautiful too. I like how this also helps make my lashes appear fuller and thicker too. I have really enjoyed testing this product and love the results. I did receive this primer at a special price to use and give my opinion on its performance.

description_text: Iso E Super is an aroma-chemical, which, on its own, is less of a fragrance than an effect. Almost transparent in colour it has a vague sweet cedarwood-like scent imparting a male, woodsy, musky type aroma. It is known as the invisible fragrance, and has also been likened to a modern day Love Potion No.9! The reason for this is that it has been known to mimic the action of human pheromones. Although not a pheromone itself, it has the effect of other people noticing you or your fragrance but not quite being able to put their finger on the reason why. This is because ordinary fragrances are designed to project themselves over a wide radius, whilst Iso E Super is designed to cling to the skin, swapping itself between opulence and simplicity, sometimes being quite noticeable, sometimes undetectable. The wearer may notice a subtle, velvety, woody note which will vanish, then re-surface after some time. More than this, she or he will notice the impact the fragrance has on other people, because Iso E Super lends an indefinable allure to the wearer. In fact, its effect is almost pheromonic.

review_title: I'm not sorry I tried it
review_text:
I like it okay, although it has some limitations.

It is somewhat stiff - I'd like it to be just a little less stiff. It reminds me of extra wide good quality packing tape, the kind that isn't too flimsy. This makes it easy to apply color to, since it doesn't flop around, but at the same time I'd like it to be a little easier to fold.

The tape is too wide. I have long hair and I like to make many thin and narrow sections for multiple colors, but because the tape is much wider than my sections, there isn't room.

I'm using Directions by La Riche', and I'm generous with the product, but some hairs get pulled, stretched, and snapped with every tape removal.

On the positive plus side, I use disposable nitrile gloves, and I'm able to pull the tape from the roll and use it without it sticking to the gloves. I found that surprisingly convenient.

I think if it were available in a narrower size, I'd like it more. If it were a bit more flexible I'd like it a lot more. I do like that I can see to make sure I've saturated all the hair.

It's okay and I think it's worth trying. Depending on how you're sectioning hair, and what products you're working with, it might work quite well for you.

review_text: I have something called Horner's Syndrome, it's some kind of crazy bizarre nerve damage in which part of my face is really dry and doesn't perspire and other areas perspire way too much. Generally, I start to apply my makeup and need to stop 3-4 times during process to gently blot the same 4 overly sweaty sections, lightly dust powder, sit with a fan, think breezy thoughts, etc. I was careful not to paint the Skin Prep on the alternate, dry areas, those areas do not perspire and can develop a parched, peely appearance. When it comes to the mirror, we notice things in so much greater detail than anyone else ever would, I realize no one else may ever notice the difference I notice. review_text:
This wax is my go to wax for my mustache. I have a thinner mustache with thin tips and this holds beautiful curls all day long as long as you don't get it wet. It will hold up to my dog's occasional kiss, but anything more, like rain, and they will fall apart immediately. With this said it makes it really easy to clean up at the end of the day. It does tend to leave droplets on the sink, but they wipe off with a damp rag.

This wax does have a dye in it, and it does cover the few greys i have in my mustache. The brown was too dark, this seems to blend a bit better and look more natural with my brown facial hair.

I have attached 2 photos so you can see the length of the mustache and the normal size of my everyday curls. If I am dressing up I will take the time to make larger curls, but they are more delicate and don't hold as long.

I find this to be super easy to keep with me, as you may find throughout the day that you may have to touch up your mustache for various reasons. The tube makes it extremely simple to do so.

With that said you do need to have water with you when you do the mustache as if you use your finger, which you will have to do to get curls, you will have to apply it with your fingers and they will be covered in the dye.

The dye is not permanent and has never stained any of my clothing.

There is a slight odor to the wax, but it's no stronger than some of the high end waxes I have tried. I continue to came back to this wax for it's simplicity and ease of use.

review_title: I paid for "CITY" brand, but received something called "WayGo."  This is false advertising.
review_text: I saw all the negative reviews, but thought I would try it anyway... less than $3 and free shipping wasn't going to break the bank.  However, all the negative reviews are accurate!  It takes a long time to dry (in the photo below, the picture was taken at about 5 minutes), and when it peels off it's inconsistent.  The first time it didn't come off all in one piece.  The second time it came off in one large piece and one tiny piece.  I would say it peels off like a thick layer of Elmer's glue peeled off when I was in elementary school.  I paid for "CITY" brand, but received something called "WayGo."  This is false advertising.  If CITY brand has changed its name, it should be updated in the description.  I agree that the smell is pleasant... but I'm not buying it for the smell.  I'm buying it protect my nails when doing nail art.  The first bottle of latex peel off nail protector was by a company called "PUEEN" and while it is more expensive (approximately $9 a bottle) it works like a dream!  I would highly recommend that to anyone who doesn't have a latex allergy.  Bottom line, unless you plan to wash WayGo off your fingers with soap and water after your manicure is completed, I would avoid this like the plague.  There, I said it.  LOL  Also, if it helps anyone else to know, I paid for this on 12/1/16 and received it on 1/6/17.

review_title: Absolutely the BEST for nail art and I've tried MANY!
review_text:
Good liquid latex is every nail artist's best friend. I decided to purchase this jar after using up my supply of prepared/bottled liquid latex varieties, and I am so glad I did. Prior to discovering Liquid Latex Fashions, I was buying liquid latex marketed as "nail art tape". In terms of package price and the consistent quality of product, I find that this is the much better option. As long as I continue to stamp, water marble and do gradient nails I will continue to use THIS. Here are the highlights as to why I think Liquid Latex Fashions is superior to all the rest:

* Package size is 4 ounces and an ample supply for simple nail art. It is smaller in real life than what it appears in the ad photos. I have been using this as my go-to for the past six months and have barely made a dent in it. I suspect that it will probably dry up before I can get through it all.
* Product is simple to decant - the large mouth on the jar makes it easy to use an infant medicine syringe to draw the liquid up and dispense into a clean nail polish bottle. (You can get the plastic medi syringes for free at the pharmacy counter - all you have to do is ask.)
* Consistency is thin/watery, which is easy to apply and dries very fast. It turns to a dark pink when it's dry. One layer works great for me, but you can add more layers if needed.
* It peels so good! Always a clean peel in one solid sheet - no bits and pieces of latex that break off. You can literally roll your fingertip across the edge and peel it off in one whole piece. No more fighting with latex removal after doing a gorgeous gradient!
* FYI: Ammonia free does not mean odorless. This product does not smell good at all. If you've used any type of liquid latex before, you know it does have a distinguishable smell. It is somewhere between fish oil and cat urine. Or a mixture of both. Yeah, it stinks to be perfectly honest. Just be forewarned.
* Pricing of this is so much more economical versus prepared varieties. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if some folks weren't just repackaging this and slapping their brand labels on it.
* The bonus to THIS particular liquid latex - it's black light reactive... so if you plan on going to an all-night rave anytime soon, you can wear this and you'll glow all night! lol ;)

🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
Highly recommended and I will most definitely repurchase when I hit tub bottom. Thanks for reading!

Seriously though, one more thing - In order to keep the latex fresh and from drying up, you should make sure to wipe any excess latex from around the neck of the jar. Keep the lid screwed on tight when not in use, and store it in a cool dry place.

review_text:
Honestly and truly, this eyebrow tint changed my life. I have naturally blonde hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes. I dye my hair regularly to a dark reddish brown, and obviously need my eyebrows and eyelashes to match so as not to look weird. I wear mascara everyday no problem and have been anyways for years, but I always hated feeling like I NEEDED to do my eyebrows before I went into public. Plus I hate feeling like they look drawn on and too done up. Beyond that, if I spent the night at anyone's house I would have to wear at least brow mascara to bed and risked looking bad when I woke up with it smeared all over my face.
I read the reviews before I used this and everyone said to leave the dye on for around 5 minutes. However the box says 2 minutes. The first time I used the dye I was freaking out a little because I thought I was messing up by leaving it on so long. DON'T WORRY. After the first time, I leave it on for closer to 10 minutes now. The dye definitely makes your brows dark, but that's what I prefer.
The first time I used this, it was before I went over to my boyfriend's house for the night. I literally was just laying in his bed smiling at how happy I was that I wasn't wearing any makeup, I felt confident in my brows looking good, and that I wouldn't have to worry about how I looked in the morning. It was such a great feeling! My eyebrows are one of my biggest insecurities and this gave me such a confidence boost!
I actually ended up opening all the little capsules and emptying them into the little bag provided and I just scoop out a little at a time to use. I did this because when I emptied an entire capsule into the little mixing pot, it made SO MUCH DYE and I ended up throwing away 3/4 of what I made. They give you 16 capsules but this still felt like a huge waste. This way I make smaller batches and have less waste and can stretch the product longer.
I'd say the only two cons of this product are that it only lasts maybe 5 days before I have to reapply, and that it's hard to apply it without staining your skin. So don't dye your eyebrows right before you leave your house, I try to do it at night and by the morning my natural oils have made the dye lift a little. By day two you can't see the stains anymore.

review_text:
Uh, hello, this product is dope AF. I have suffered my whole life from pretty sparse and invisible colored brows. It's weird, because my hair is pretty dark brown, but my brows look like fishing line and I look like an alien with no makeup on them. I was snooping around the internet doing some research on microblading, which is basically like tattooing on your eyebrows, but it's pretty expensive, and only lasts a few years, and also I don't really trust other people to semi-permanently choose the shape of my brows. I stumbled across this product on Instagram I think and decided to give it a shot.

If you regularly draw on your eyebrows, then applying this will be a breeze. If you have dark hair and wear your brows dark, then you don't really even have to worry too much about how long you keep this product on. I usually do 3 applications at about 7 minutes at a time each time I dye my brows.

I noticed in other reviews that there was some discrepancy on how long this product lasts, and I think I figured out where the difference is coming from. If you have pretty full and nicely shaped brows, but they are light colored and you want them darker, and you are only using this product to dye the ACTUAL HAIRS of your eyebrows, a single application of this will last for weeks. HOWEVER, if you have thin, sparsely furred brows and are using this product to dye the SKIN under and around your actual brow hairs (like drawing or tattooing would do) then this will really only last between 2 and 4 days depending on what you're putting on your face and what kind of activities (like sweating) you are doing.

Either way it is still worth it. It is so nice to wake up in the morning with eyebrows instead of looking like Bob Geldoff in The Wall. I also get about 3 applications from each little "pill" so this product should last a good long while before I have to reorder. Overall very good purchase that I would recommend to anyone who wants darker, fuller brows.

review_title: In less than 24 hours I'm obsessed!
review_text:
I've had this day cream for less than 24 hours... so I may be jumping the gun but I'm already so amazed I just had to review!

I am in my mid-20's with sensitive dry skin that breaks out in zits and/or hives if you simply just look at it wrong. My previous face cream has either been discontinued or moved to some obscure unfindable website. So I took a leap of faith trying this rose day cream. And oh my goodness, I am so happy I did! My face has never been so soft and clear and... glowy! I feel like I have an entirely new face, and in under 24 hours no less!

This cream is very concentrated. I only need to gently tap the cream with my fingertip once or twice to cover my entire face and neck. review_title: I finally found my holy grail dark green hair color! I love the muted shade range.
review_text:
I have been looking for a dark, truly green hair dye for ages. Most dark greens skew hard teal,and mixing colors to get the desired shade usually fades to blue annoyingly fast. Green Tomato is the color of tomato vines and is very pigmented—it's such a dark green that it looks almost black when it comes out of the tube. It has a gray undertone rather than a blue or yellow one. I love this color. It's a muted, deep green that fades to a dark mossy tone after many washes. The result is a more natural, "lived-in" color right from the start.

The dye has a gel-like consistency that makes it very spreadable. I have shoulder-length, fine hair. Even using this completely undiluted and unmixed, I will get at least a dozen uses out of this one tube. I've used it undiluted to achieve a dark green that passes for black in dim or soft lighting. (Side Note: be careful to avoid applying undiluted dye directly to your scalp, this stains your skin quite badly.) I've diluted it with white, silicone-free conditioner to create a pastel version. Using a lot of conditioner creates a slightly grainy mixture, but it hasn't affected the quality or longevity of the results. I've also mixed it with several other brands of dye (e.g. Pravana, Iroiro, La Riche Directions, and Bigen Vivid Shades) with no issues and positive results. It smells sort of like markers, with a hint of perfume. It's not particularly terrible, but it's one of the worst-smelling brands of semi-permanent hair color I've come across.

I really think Sarangsae is doing something special with the shade range they offer. I've used over a dozen brands in all the colors of the rainbow, but nobody else is creating such soft, understated colors. It's not too hard for me to achieve a soft pastel (either by using a pastel dye or diluting a dark dye) but dark shades are usually extremely bright. I love mixing my own colors, and the hardest thing to achieve is a muted dark hue. I've added silver dyes,the Pravana Vivids "black" additive, and/or small amounts of opposing shades (i.e., a dab of pink or light orange to a green to tone it down) with various success. I'm really excited to try some of their other muted colors in the future, like Black Rose, Deep Grey, or Mustard Yellow. If they can make a truly soft, deep, dark green, they can probably make any shade!

review_title: Beautiful, works great, smooth combing, nice weight, but is it ebony?
review_text:
I would give this five stars if I believed it were actually ebony wood. I ordered it because it was in the description as ebony and I loved the carved pattern. However, when this arrived, inside the package, the plastic sheet labels this as sandalwood. However, it does not have a sandalwood scent, either. Actual ebony is pitch black, other than the outer shell, of which is brown like these combs. In conclusion if this is ebony this would be of the outer hull of the ebony trunk, not the inner black section. Ebony grows in Africa and a striped version in Indonesia. Ebony is dense enough to sink in water and takes a lot of work to dry out for crafting.

Now the comb itself is wonderfully carved, a big reason why I ordered over some of the other wooden combs here on Amazon. It combs through my hair very smoothly, no static or hair pulling like with brushes or plastic. As far as function and appearance it is beautiful and comes very well packaged in a plastic bag, then a velveteen bag that is placed inside a black envelope and tied with a ribbon. Amazon sent it separate from the rest of my order so it would remain safe and intact. The wood itself has a nice weight, but is not too heavy.

Would I recommend this comb? Yes, but keep in mind, while wood, I am not positive this is actual ebony other than maybe the outer hull of the ebony tree, but I suspect something else. I would have to take this to a wood expert to know for sure, and who has the money for that, these days? So, enjoy it for it's appearance and smooth combing.

I absolutely recommend for sensitive or dry skin.

review_text:
I bought this powder specifically to use under my eyes. What makes it different from most loose powders is that it contains cornstarch, giving it a smooth finish without being too drying. The only other loose powders I've been able to find that contain cornstarch are the Ben Nye Luxury Powders, and the Col-Lab Set the Stage loose powder from Sally's, which is sold on their website only. I've tried samples of the Ben Nye Luxury Powders in a few colors and liked them, but decided to try something different, and a little cheaper.

I apply this powder in one of two different ways. If I want a minimal makeup look, I'll use my ELF blush brush to pat the powder under my eyes, tapping off any excess from the brush before application. If I want my undereyes to look especially smooth, and my deep tear troughs less noticeable, I use a dry foam wedge sponge to pick up the powder, then stamp it under my eyes, and gently brush off the excess after a minute or two. It does not make my undereye area look or feel dry. Sometimes I use it all over my face, if I'd rather not use my usual matte pressed powder. I have fair skin, so the white color appears translucent on my skin, but I'm not sure how someone with deeper skin would fare.

Because I use this powder sparingly, this jar should last me a long time!

8/25/18 - My review is LONG past due. Many years ago, I started using Pampers Baby Wipes. (I had gotten sick with bad dose of diarrhea. Excessive wiping cause some soreness.) Afterwards, I decided I liked the cleanliness and bought a very large quantity. Three years later, the type I bought were no longer available. The remaining Pampers were outrageously expensive, so I bought another, cheaper, generic brand. Over the next year, I got into a bit of an argument with my husband about flushing the wipes. There was never a problem and the wipes I used were supposed to be biodegradable, but still, my husband insisted I not flush them. A few years ago, I ran across this spray wash and bought it. At first, I had intended to make my own wipes, but never got around to it. Abruptly, I ran out of my generic wipes. I'd grown so accustomed to using wipes, I didn't want to go without, so I pulled out the spray, and sprayed the toilet tissue and used it. For at least the last 2 years, this has been my answer to baby wipes and the conflict of flushing them, biodegradable or not.

This California Baby Diaper Area Wash is a wonderful product. I have an unusually good nose and I always feel (and smell) fresh and clean. I'm a bit of an older woman (Some would say I've entered my "golden years.") and I've never had a female infection of any type. I realize a lot of this is due to genes, but some of depends on cleanliness. This personal spray wash is an excellent way to avoid discomfort and remain clean and fresh throughout the day, every day.

I hope the creator doesn't mind my comments. I know it was developed for babies and there was a time when it was unavailable. But, I'm not a pushover and I'm not one to give good reviews for something that I haven't found worthy of my praise. I don't know the creator and I haven't been compensated, in any way, for my review. My comments are strictly my own.

review_text: First time in 20 years I've transitioned from a liquid concealer to a powder, the coverage is obviously not the same but this is by far the best performing powder I've ever had. I'm lucky in that my face at it's not-the-most-tan tiny works well with the light color but I can see how the limited color choices can be a deal breaker for some. It's smooth and not cakey, it blends well, feels weightless, and stands up to sweating and long work days with great shine prevention and it doesn't come off easily (a little when you blow your nose etc). I do not like the porcelain doll look and this works well for me for evening out tones.  I am 35 and have very sensitive skin, several minor facial scars, and occasional adult acne and this doesn't have any negative effects on my skin at all. It washes off easily with gentle face wash. It allows for a few spot touches of stick concealer, blends well, and holds well. Mine arrived with no breaks/cracks and the sponge works well. I really like the protective inner plastic case between the powder and the lid and sponge. Will buy again! I previously used Revlon, Covergirl, Neutrogena, and JUNGSAEMMOOL Essential Star-cealer Foundation which I was happy with the first time and then the following two were slimy and just not working well. For reference my current face tone is a revlon 300-310, a covergirl 705-710, and Starcealer Light. After peak summer I'm a more 310-320, 710-715, and Starcealer Medium (almost, its still a little dark for me).

Still, this device is new to me so for now I don’t go much beyond the orbital bone- where I apply my night time eye cream. I definitely recommend the smaller eye attachment head for Glo Pro users and rate it 5 stars.

I wasn’t provided a Glo Pro device and this review is only of the eye attachment head. Still, I’m sure people wonder if Glo Pro works. I’ve used a Glo Pro about a month, twice a week, and don’t feel I’ve used it long enough to know. I’m in my 50’s and my skin does happen to look good lately. I don’t see dramatic changes, but my skin seems firmer and my fine lines around my eyes and elsewhere seem less noticeable. But I feel I need to use Glo Pro longer to decide if it’s the device, my skin care products or both that are providing a benefit. I do like Glo Pro enough to keep using it.

review_title: Two 5 STAR and Two 4 STAR Fragrances- some are sure to please every man
review_text:
English Laundry Men's 4 Piece 20ml Coffret is a truly wonderful men’s cologne set. You are getting four fragrances- rated 4 and 5 STARS all in one box. The fragrances rated by me are based on my years spent working in a cosmetic factory. I will list each fragrance separately.

ARROGANT- With top notes of bergamot and cedar you get a woodsy freshness to the scent. The middle notes of coriander and lavender bring a warm, clean freshness. At the base are sandalwood, amber and musk bringing a warm, sensual, spicy scent. All together, you get a spicy, warm, woodsy scent with a distinctive freshness to it. This light, sensual scent lasts all day and smells wonderful on almost every man, so 5 STARS.

OXFORD BLEU- The top notes of mint and lemon add a citrus freshness. The middle notes of iris and geranium bring a very light floral scent. The base adds sandalwood and vanilla for a woodsy delicious scent. All together, this scent is light, with an undertone bit of floral and clean citrus and a nice light woodsy smell. This light, woodsy fragrance smells fabulous on almost every man and does last long for 5 STARS.

RIVIERA- With top notes of lemon, bergamot, lime and cedar, you get a refreshing citrus/woods scent. In the middle are jasmine, patchouli, vetiver, lavender and mandarin- most of these were used in the 60's sexy, warm, earthy scents. At the base notes are nutmeg and coumarin to add some spice. This is not for every man, but for a man who likes a more vibrant scent. These scents are very noticeable and not light, being a very woodsy, earthy, warm fragrance with a touch of zest. 4 STARS.

NOTTING HILL- The top notes begin with bergamot, lemon and lime for a clean, natural scent. Then the middle notes have bolder peppercorn and jasmine bringing a rose/herbal scent. At the bottom are cedarwood, sandalwood, amber and a powdery musk for a very potent woodsy, animal musky scent. This is definitely not for every man being very heavy scents. There is nothing light about this fragrance. 4 STARS.

With four interesting fragrances, two being light and two being heavy, every man is sure to find one he will like. Lighter scents always smell wonderful on almost every man and the bolder scents smell great on a man depending on how his chemistry goes with the bolder fragrances. 4 ½ STARS.

review_title: Great scent, great lather. And a great price (at WallyWorld).
review_text:
Palmer's/E.T. Browne has a lot of above-average products in its line. This is one of them, for sure.

The scent is scrumptious. Not much like "coconut sun-tan oil at the beach" … much more like "fresh coconut cream pie desert!"

I say above-average because, if you scour the ingredient list on Palmer's products, you will typically find SOME natural & luxurious ingredients … and also some fairly common chemicals. So many of their products are of a higher quality than common store-shelf items … but not exactly in the category of seriously premium and/or upscale products.

For example, this product's main ingredient is Sodium olefin sulfonate. That's a common ingredient in bath & body products that used to make them lather. And Palmer's has been very generous with it, in that this shampoo really REALLY lathers up! The next major ingredient is coconut fruit extract. Many manufacturers won't use coconut oils or extracts in their bath & body products because straight-up palm oils and extracts are cheaper. After that there's a list of many other common chemical sounding ingredients. But also there's coconut oil, Tahitian gardenia extract, keratin-protein and glycerin. Those too are premium ingredients that common bath & body products usually won't contain. And this shampoo contains NO sulfates, parabens, mineral oil, dyes, gluten or phthalates.

That's a lot of quality, given the price … that being $4.36 at WallyWorld for a 14 ounce bottle… and, as of this writing, with instant "$2 off" coupons attached. That's a lot less expensive than other "big brand name" shampoos that offer less and cost more.

There's also a matching body wash product. In use, and in the ingredient list, they are almost exactly the same product. And there's a matching bar soap, though I found it far less interesting - meh - than this shampoo and its matching body wash.

This shampoo seems far better suited for dry hair; it conditions, moisturizes and protects. But I have oily hair. So I sometimes resort to using my bar soap on my hair as a first pass, to "cut through" a lot of the oil, before actually using this shampoo as a second application.

In any case, for a mere $2.36, you can pick up a bottle of this stuff at WallyWorld and see how this shampoo suits you yourself.

review_title: While Subjective, I Do Think My Skin Looks Better Using Glo Pro Regularly W/ Good Products
review_text:
While I think evaluating the results is subjective, I enjoy micro needling with my Glo Pro a lot and do believe it makes my skin look better. I used Glo Pro regularly for about 2-1/2 months, 2-3 times a week. I’m 57 and felt my skin did look particularly good with regular use. While results weren’t dramatic in that my wrinkles didn’t magically disappear, I feel the overall appearance of my skin seemed brighter, firmer and some lines seemed less noticeable. Around my eyes and cheeks aren’t big problem areas (except dark circles), but my fine lines looked virtually nonexistent in those areas and I feel I looked more refreshed and my skin looked more taut. The frown lines by my mouth are my worst issue and those didn’t improve as much as I hoped, but I did think the lines seemed less noticeable and the area seemed less saggy or firmer to me.

I decided to take a break of about a month to see if I stopped if I’d notice a difference. I don’t think my skin looks as good as it did when using Glo Pro regularly. I feel I look less refreshed, my frown lines look worse and my skin seems kind of dull. I can’t speak to the science of whether micro needing really increases collagen production (or if it can damage the skin), or if my benefit is because it increases absorption of my arsenal of serums and creams. But I do think I looked better from use and my skin doesn’t look as good since I stopped. It’s a tool that I’ve gone back to using, and I do really like using a lot. I apply quality serums and creams within 60 seconds of using Glo Pro and do think I get bigger benefits from my products. I personally avoid using AHA and retinol products after Glo Pro as they’re too irritating for my sensitive skin.

I don’t find Glo Pro painful to use. The needles feel just a little prickly and give me a slight burning sensation. But it’s not uncomfortable or painful and hasn’t caused me any excessive redness, irritation or bleeding. I’ve seen videos of bleeding caused by micro needling done by professionals and read that going that deep isn’t required for micro needling to work. I only use Glo Pro at night and never wake with any redness or irritation. I do use the Glo Pro Pads after I cleanse to sanitize in order to avoid bacteria spread as I got a few blemishes after I ran out but don’t get blemishes using the pads (and alcohol is much too harsh for my dry skin). I always keep the included spritz bottle filled with alcohol and spray the head after every use. While subjective, I do feel my skin looks better from using Glo Pro regularly with good treatment products and rate it 5 stars.

review_text:
99J is a much darker red than pictured, but a very beautiful color. Even my pics look too light, almost auburn & not the very deep burgundy or black cherry color I received. At first glance, this appears unusable due to the very large seam showing in back & I almost sent it back. But I sprayed on liquid hair gel at the roots, teased it with my fingers, & used hair dryer heat to make the roots stick straight up, giving them lift, & also making the hair also flip backwards, which seemed impossible to do at first glance. I have now managed to cover that awful seam, transformed it from stiff, flat & boring to full, natural-looking & silky with no seams showing anywhere.
I may order another one to color a little lighter to wear when my red shade fades. I will take a pic of what it first looks like. I have colored many hair pieces, sometimes lightening them first with a color remover like color zap. I also curl them to match my own hair. Will attach styled pics of front, top, back, & underneath. review_text: This tape is wonderful and very strong. I have very fine thinning hair and this tape has held up for 6 weeks now with no slipping. I think the confusion and bad reviews might come from people using this tape with wefts rather than tape in extensions.  I have worn tape in extensions for years and what I do is apply the sandwich method then I do 3 quick clamps with my flat iron. What I think really makes the difference is that when the tapes are still hot from the flat iron I use a pair of needle nose pliers and squeeze along the width of the tape on each side. This really squished it together. Then I wait at least 72 hours to shampoo my hair after the initial install. I always remove the tape that comes on my extensions because when I color them to match my hair they usually get all gross anyway.

I ordered a number of sample colognes from eBay recently after reading an article about the top rated colognes available on the market. This one was on this list and it is easy to see why. It's difficult to review colognes for obvious reasons, but I have a collection of about 10-15 fragrances and have sampled dozens of other ones, mostly referrals by Jeremy Fragrance on YouTube. I have never smelled a scent that lit my eyes up like this one did when I first sprayed it. It is the perfect blend of sweetness and masculinity, with subtle notes you'll catch whiffs of throughout the day that you didn't notice before. I think it is definitely a summer-only fragrance because of how colorful and bright it is. It has great staying power and a little goes a long way. Wear this on a first date and even if you're dull, you'll still probably get a second one because of this fragrance.

review_text:
So I'm gonna start by saying I am a very skeptical person, and I'm cheap. I hate spending money if I don't have to. I ran into a friend a few weeks ago, she was meeting her Monat distributor to pick up more product when I saw her. I have heard of this stuff for a couple years now, but have always remained skeptical and not wanting to fork out the money to try it. So I asked her what she thought about the product, and if there was a big enough difference to really make it worth it. And she went on and on to me about her love for Monat and all the differences she's noticed. So I thought about it, and almost made the first initial purchase (which would have been a minimum of $100 off the bat, but they do have a 30 day money back guarantee no matter how much you use of the product). I talked myself out of purchasing, because lets face it, $100 is expensive. So I did some research, and talked to my friend a couple more times.
Finally I got on ebay, and found sample packs. I figured, I could waste $10 easier than $100. So I purchased the Revive Shampoo samples. And I did just as my friend suggested, I washed twice, instead of once. I also decided to try the Revitalize Conditioner (purchased those too). Let me say, after shampooing, my hair was dry feeling (I could tell the difference in the shower), but when I put the conditioner in, it was like it transformed completely. I got out of the shower, still unsure what I think. I started drying my hair (I chose not to put any other product in just to see). AND OMG. My hair was so vibrant, different, my fly-away's were staying down, it felt a little more weighted than usual (which I LOVE because I have the thinnest and finest hair ever, so it gets static easily). I was in disbelief I could pull this off without my usual leave in conditioner and oil and volumizing mousse. Usually I have to get out of the shower, spray in the oil, spray in the conditioner, mix in the mousse and then style. Not with Monat though. The next day, my hair was still nice. I was still skeptical though. Now I'm 2 weeks in, and I'm still in love. People around me are noticing the difference in my hair too. I don't feel like I have to throw it up in a pony tail either like I usually would. It's soft, easy to manage, looks nicer and fuller. I love it. I also decided to get some Root lifting stuff from Monat, just to see if I would love that too. I will say, it's not bad. It does give me a little more volume, not as much as I would like, but not bad! :) I've only tried that twice so far though! :) I do plan on becoming a VIP now and making that $100 purchase, and now I can't wait to try the Wonder lash stuff! I hope my review is helpful to those out there who are skeptical like me.

review_text:
WOW!! These are good. They are very similar in style to all the other dermaplaning razors out there, but they are longer than any I have used. The blade is just a hair under 2". Pun intended. One of the popular blades among beauty conscious people (pictured) is around 1.5". Many are 1" or less. SO, keep this in mind for where you want to use this and if you are comfortable with that length of blade. Otherwise it is all very similar.

I like that this 5 pack is contained within a box. Many are on a flat piece of cardboard with molded plastic around them. Makes it too easy to lose one, misplace one.. they just fall out of package when opened. This box will nicely store the remainder. I won't lose these among my other beauty goodies.

I have no idea what it says on the box. The sticker on the box says Made in China. The box says, Made in Japan. I can't read anything else.

Handle is short- I think adds to precision of use. The longer blade makes it harder to get the eyebrow area. For that, I would go with a smaller, angled razor. For larger areas of face (or other body areas), this large blade is nice. As with any blade, BE CAREFUL. And don't over use it- a dull blade can be as dangerous and damaging as a sharp blade.

The blade is indeed sharp. I usually use a regular razor (like for shaving legs) to shave my face. I have pale skin and dark hair, so I have always preferred to just shave off my hair. No, it doesn't grow back thicker or darker. But it sure makes the face nice and smooth- great for make up looking good, for skin care setting in nicely, for exfoliation- for overall health of skin. A leg razor is fine, less likely to cut.. but a straight razor provides an extra close shave (if careful). I love these for taking care of upper lip area, and for eyebrow area.. but is taking some getting used to since it is a longer blade than others I use.

I'll still use them though! They're very nice and durable clips, but I think I'll buy medium-sized ones in the future.

review_text: I'm someone with extremely thick and stick straight hair.  My hair loses curl within an hour of me fixing it.  I've tried other rotating curling irons and haven't had much success with them, so I didn't have very high expectations for this beach waver.  I have been pleasantly surprised.  Once I got the hang of it, I found it to be pretty easy to use.  It features buttons that allow you to chooses which direction you would like to curl each section of hair, and a Home button that after each use, and after the previous section of hair is no longer attached, allows the barrel to return to a neutral starting point.  I ran into an issue the first few times I used it, which was accidentally hitting the home button while my hair was still around the barrel.  This caused the hair to get very tight and the barrel to press up against the scalp.  This is very easy to do and I definitely think a design change should take place to correct this issue.  The barrel is long enough for my medium-long hair and I can see it needing to be used more than once up and down the length of long hair.  The curling iron gets up to 410 degrees max, which works pretty well on my thick hair.  I've tried fixing my hair in different ways after using it, to see which method holds the curls longer.  I still have an issue with my hair losing the curls a bit to quickly but it's remedied by using styling products before and after curling it.  To be honest, I think this beach waver is very overpriced.  Maybe the results would be better for someone with thinner hair but I don't think I'd pay more than $50 for this curling iron.  Nice results, but the design flaws make this a product I won't reach for that often.

review_title: Works on my notoriously impossible to curl hair!
review_text: So, I approached buying a new styling tool very cautiously, since my hair notoriously does not hold a curl. But I just cut it short and really thought this length would be super cute with a little texture to it. I wanted results but didn't want to spend a lot, and this product delivered. I opted for this textured style of wand because it promises to deliver different styles of curls (and otherwise I don't really know how to do that). I find it a bit tricky to wrap hair just around the raised sections (my only reason for a 4 rather than 5 star rating), but if I just sort of wrap haphazardly, it naturally falls over the raised sections near the top and into the depressions toward the end of the hair, which gives the perfect textured curl. This gets much hotter than the cheap Conair curling iron I had before this, which means my hair actually holds the style (sometimes for days!) and that I don't have to hold each curl for very long, making curling my whole head actually doable as part of my normal morning routine. I just use a little light hold heat protectant spray with this before styling, and nothing else after this, and I've got super cute voluminous bouncy waves.
