review_text:
Pros:

-Rotating cord.
-Pretty shade of pink.
-LED screen shows "off" when the crimper is plugged in and turned off. This is a good reminder to unplug.
-Good temperature display that updates you as the crimper is heating up.
-Great price for a quality product.
-Locking mechanism to keep crimper closed when not in use.
-Not easy to burn yourself on this.
-Cord comes with velcro so that you can wrap it up when traveling or storing.
-Instructions include a temperature guide for some hair types (i.e., fine hair/not fine hair and damaged/not damaged hair).
-Dual voltage, which is good for travel.

Cons:

-Instructions do not come with tips for the actual process of crimping your hair.
-The demo videos on the Amazon page are not helpful...and not what I want my hair to look like. You have to Google Youtube influencer videos if you want to find out how to actually achieve a nice wave/crimp. I have yet to be able to achieve the deep, romantic waves I was hoping for (like the ones advertised).
-Instructions have a quick note (with no elaboration) stating that the crimper doubles as a straightener. I'm not sure what this means or how that would work.
-It's NOT easy to get a good crimp. It will take practice and googling.
-My hair, which usually holds curls really well, doesn't hold this shape well. I'd recommend a lot of hair spray and patience.
-Pictures on the Amazon page of results are not accurate. The videos, while more disappointing, are more accurate.
-There's a brief piece of instruction on the Amazon page that seems quite important. Unfortunately, I have no idea what it means, and there's nothing anywhere to help me understand it: "Hair Curling Iron 2 in 1: Unlocking the barrel for deep wavy curls and locking the barrel for big curls on long hair." Also: "Lock the iron for Big Curls: Wrap a hair section for seconds, then repeat it with all your hairs." I'd love to know how to do this.
-Not a con really, but just FYI for American users: The temperature is in celsius.

The product is well-designed as hair tools go, and the price is quite reasonable. The instructions are lacking, and I find the advertising to be a bit misleading. I will still experiment with the crimper, and I will continue to look up crimping tutorial videos in hopes that I can get the big, deep waves advertised.

review_title: Not quite there yet, buyer beware
review_text: Full disclosure, I bought this at the Container Store for the same price listed here. I’ve had it maybe 6-8 months and I loved the look and it stuck VERY well (you’ve got to clean your shower!). But over the past months it has consistently gotten cloudier and cloudier and as many have mentioned it’s not anti-fog at all. I thought maybe there was some soap scum or something similar so I pulled it down this morning. Little bit of mold behind it because of the tile gap and that stained the rubber. The mirror is not glass it’s a light feeling plastic coated thing. That explained the slight wave in the mirror. Cleaned it this evening with rubbing alcohol and warm water and afterwards it was nearly non-reflective. I threw it away because it’s useless now. A friend mentioned that the polycarbonate used doesn’t like water and heat and that may have caused a reaction with the mirror (defeats the purpose though, I’m not taking boiling hot showers). Possibly the chemicals used to clean my shower messed it up, but for $15 I would have expected that common cleaners wouldn’t have done that in less than a year. Overall, product needs more work, certainly not worth $15.

That being said, though, it is far more aesthetically appealing, user-friendly, and gentler than the traditional pumice stones or foot graters.

A protective storage case would be a great addition to this item. I saved all the packaging and have been placing the file back into the plastic packaging tray and then placing that tray back into the outer plastic packaging box. Something similar to a travel bar soap container or a retainer case would be perfect (slimmer, of course, to fit the file)! The storage case with drainage holes for drying would minimize the risk of breaking the file during cleaning, drying, and storing it. For the current price point, I personally think a reusable storage case should be included.

All that aside, my only real concern, and the reason for the current rating, is that my feet actually felt and looked dryer and rougher several days to a week after the first use. I realize this may be due to my own user error, as I followed the exfoliation with my usual moisturization regimen. It is reasonable to assume I should have taken extra steps to protect and care for me feet immediately following the exfoliation, as the delicate, softer skin was exposed. So, I am going to try it again, this is over-moisturizing and wearing plush socks for the few days afterward. I will update my review with my new results!

Overall, I currently recommend this foot file. I find it to be worth trying out, and is a better alternative to the more abrasive methods. I have included photos showing the packaging and tray in which I keep it stored, as well as close-ups of the smooth top size and gritty underside. Hope they help!

review_text:
A lot of the early reviews for this are going to be negative because they shipped the way-too-thick conditioner with a pump-top that doesn't work with it. They should have made it less thick, or shipped it in a wide-mouth jar you could scoop it out of like face cream, but since they didn't, the easiest thing is to switch the lids. The pump-top works fine on the shampoo. The press-open top on the conditioner is still a bother, but turning it upside down and rapping it on something to drive the conditioner to the opening does work. Don't break it.

Supposing they'll fix this, how's the shampoo and conditioner?

Well, speaking of face cream, the first thing I noticed was the unusual fragrance. Unusual for shampoo and conditioner, I mean. It reminds me of some face and other skin creams, sweet and vaguely flowery. It's light and pleasant enough, though some men may want something more traditional for them. And possibly those with extra-sensitive noses may be able to detect the garlic in the shampoo. (Yes, garlic. There are actually garlic shampoos, with a lot more garlic than here, some of which claim not to smell like garlic.) No garlic in the conditioner.

The shampoo is thick and lathers well and cleans well.

The ultra-thick conditioner, once you manage to get it on your hair, is fine, leaves my hair soft and combable.

The ingredients (given below) look fairly conventional for the most part, a mix of synthetic and natural. For the shampoo, the collagen is the 17th ingredient by weight, so under 6% (probably far less), and the keratin is 28th, under 4% (probably far less). For the conditioner, the keratin is the 12th ingredient, meaning it could be as much as 8% (though again probably far less). For all I know that's plenty for what they're supposed to do.

There's a lot of plant stuff in the shampoo, some only given in Latin, so here's the translation of the rest. Besides the acai, Matricaria (German chamomile), echinacea, garlic, lemon, sage, and spirulina, the shampoo has:

Argania spinosa = argan
Symphytum officinale = comfrey
Trigonella foenum-graecum = fenugreek
Quercus alba = white oak
Viola tricolor = viola, or Johnny jumpup

The conditioner also has some argan and acai, and adds:

Fucus vesiculosus = bladderwrack (a seaweed)

Some people prefer not to have the amodimethicone, here in both the shampoo and conditioner, a silicone some say is hard to rinse out, though others praise it for its conditioning effects particularly with bleached hair and for its limited buildup.

Similarly, there's dimethicone in the conditioner, which some find to build up over time, while others don't seem to notice any trouble with that and enjoy its conditioning and emollient qualities.

To apply correctly and have the mirror effect, you must adhere to nail tech guidelines!!

1. Wash & scrub your nails with a nail brush.

2. Dry your nails!

3. Apply a base coat. This is VERY important to have a filled in base on your nails. I use Mia's.

4. Apply one thin coat to each nail.

5. Use a nail corrector pen or small brush dipped in acetone to remove any on cuticles.

6. Go back to first nail painted and apply a second, thicker coat. Repeat on other nails.

7. Repeat step 5.

8. Apply your choice of top coat. I use Mia's in my salon.

review_title: The only brand I am brand loyal to
review_text:
My husband got this for me.

Honestly? I'm not a "brand" kind of girl. I just use whatever works and typically shun designer things and extremely overpriced branded things, but I've learned that sometimes a company CAN earn your loyalty. Essie is amazing nail polish! It's pigmented, smooth, the cut of the brush makes painting your nails extremely easy (even on my left hand which I am usually USELESS at!) and even without a clear top coat it lasts so much longer than other brands I've tried. I have small hands and petite nails, so a lot of brushes just make a mess even if I'm very careful, but I've never had an issue with an Essie brush. The cut of a nail polish brush may not be something a lot of people think about but once you find the right brush fit for you, you'll notice a H U G E difference!

The colors Essie offers are unique and beautiful, many of them universal for all skin tones from the palest porcelain to the deepest and richest ebony. And any brand that uses inclusive models for all their campaigns is alright with me, too.

All in all, I've ditched every other nail polish brand and I'm sticking to Essie from now on.

Oh, and Let It Glow is a really beautiful coral color with a golden shimmer that's perfect for spring and summer and the metallic effect is soft enough that even ridged nails can use it without it highlighting texture!

To apply correctly and have the mirror effect, you must adhere to nail tech guidelines!!

1. Wash & scrub your nails with a nail brush.

2. Dry your nails!

3. Apply a base coat. This is VERY important to have a filled in base on your nails. I use Mia's.

4. Apply one thin coat to each nail.

5. Use a nail corrector pen or small brush dipped in acetone to remove any on cuticles.

6. Go back to first nail painted and apply a second, thicker coat. Repeat on other nails.

7. Repeat step 5.

8. Apply your choice of top coat. I use Mia's in my salon.

If you can't get the same results, you're either not putting a base and top coat on or you're using too much on your first coat. Enjoy!!

review_text:
Can't go wrong with Cica cream, and at this price it is a bargain.

Cica cream is soothing and hydrating and is especially great if you have easily irritated or sensitive skin. It can really be used by anyone with any type of skin, or skin conditions. It is just a good all around cream. It typically contains centella asiatica, the star of the soothing ingredients. Not sure how much is in this, but it states 50% of the product

It is even nice to use this when you just want to give your skin a break from other products, or if your skin has been stressed (environmentally), or if your skin is reacting to something and you need a soothing cream to get through until your skin settles down.

I usually use it on my face (in winter) or hands all year, but especially lately. While I always wash my hands often, the past few months I have been using commercial anti bacterial soaps which are much more drying than some-- using CICA cream helps keep my hands looking and feeling healthy). SO yeh, I am mostly loving it as a post hand washing cream.

Before this one from Village11Factory, there were two other cica products I have used in my life, both a bit pricier. So I think this is good one to try if you are seeking to try it out, and want a simple but effective skin soothing product but don't want to break the bank. The difference is usually what else is in it and sometimes a little difference in texture.. This one is the lightest of all that I have tried, leans more gel like. It is nice and light- one I think is nice for summer. I think I prefer my slightly heavier, creamier one (But 3x pricier for same amount) for winter use-- when I need the extra support in cold, skin chapping weather. OH yeh, this is good stuff for lips too. It isn't a huge tube, so it could be carried in a coat pocket or purse, no problem.

I have already told several people similarly afflicted like me about this effective, nicely-fragranced pain remedy.

review_title: Please - just go buy a topcoat.
review_text:
Oh my word- no.

Okay- so this looked like a wonderful beginner kit. I am not a beginner, but I was excited to have everything in a tiny package- something easy to pull out with friends but with high quality results.

I got a friend, we opened the box and assumed I'd be ready to do her nails without getting my nail kit.

Nope.

The first sept (as it always is) was to clean buff and shape the nail- nothing included to do that.

I thought- okay- no big deal.

I got my stuff out and took care of it. I then applied their prep product- Nail dehydrator- all good.

I started to plug in the nail light, so I’d be ready after we apply the first coat- but this kit didn't include a plug- just a usb cord. (sigh) I got up again- and got an extra usb plug I had. Now slightly annoyed because this is supposed to be a ready kit-

but hey-- really-- not a huge deal.

Then I applied the base coat. Whew- runny. I wasn’t impressed with it’s consentaneity. But maybe it’d perform well?

Then I tried to cure it. Cue the light--

Oh, my word their nail lamp is horrible.

It’s very cheap looking- only fits four fingers- not the thumb at the same time, and really feels off- like the break into shards plastic, not the bendy kind. (I was still trying to accept this as a no big deal point but the red flags were slapping me in the face.)

I read the pamphlet to see how long it needed to cure- the pamphlet said "cure for the appropriate time" or something just a vague. I read the nail polish, to find the appropriate time- nope. I looed over the box- nothing.

We used the lamp like 5 times and finally got her base coat cured. Then we had to do the same with just her thumb. I have nail lights that cost three bucks that work better than this thing. I’m not kidding. In fact- I use single nail lights that only cure one nail at a time—and this was SLOWER!

Okay- that was over.

Where is the red polish?

The box says: “Step two apply polish” and it has a picture of the polish- a red polish, they name it like it’s included.

It’s not.

This starter kit isn’t much of a START without a polish-

but Okay- my nail kit to save the day.

I pulled out a blush pink gel that always does me right.

But the base coat is weird. The polish is almost clumping on the nail. It applies a tad bit patchy. I get that not all formulas work together—but they DIDN’T GIVE ME a polish to work with so theirs- in theory- should be mostly universal. I didn’t know I was intended to buy-one polishe- AND their kit to make this happen.

I try to cure MY gel polish tin their lamp.
(thank goodness my friend is a very laid-back person- she was amazing about this, laughing with me--) I was itching to pull out a good lamp but I didn’t, so I’d give this a true test.
(Or because I wanted to test my patience. Two birds one stone)

Now—here is the saving grace—

the top coat is wonderful.

It works like some of my best top coats- it leaves that perfect glassy look and it applies like a dream.

Later I used the same top coat on my nails- and it worked just as well without the weird base coat and the horrible lamp and a totally different brand of nail polish.

THIS WHOLE KIT AND THE ONLY THING THEY HAVE GOING FOR IT IS THE TOP COAT!
Now I get why this has good reviews—it’s the gel top coat.

No wonder it lasts- I can only guess Red Carpet knows their top coat is fantastic, so they threw a bunch of bad apples in here –aware beginners won’t know any better.

Please. You can buy wonderful topcoats for 10-20 bucks NOT 50 OF YOUR HARD-EARNED DOLLARS- This is such a sad waste- and they don’t even throw in a file, or a plug in or red polish?

I have more stuff coming from this brand—things I got before I tried this-- that I’m going to be trying-
I really hope this is their only issue... we shall see. 

I hope this review was helpful because I don’t want your money wasted. :(

review_text:
I bought my first box years ago (when I seem to remember it being the old packaging being labeled as brow safe?). I just finished up another box (3rd? 4th?) and noticed that it’s not meant to be used on the brows. It’s not difficult to keep far away from your eyes, just exercise caution.

I used to apply it for the recommended couple of minutes and got decent results, but now that I’m used to the performance I’ve left it on for as long as 40 minutes and have had the same color payoff but much longer lasting color. I have clear blonde brows despite being a natural dark brunette, so anything I can do to prevent fading helps.

Recommendations:
- Block/outline your brows with a white eyeliner before applying so you can just fill in the shape without having to be too precise with the actual dye- this also keeps skin staining within the area of the brow and less noticeable
- Dye at night or when you can stay in for a couple of days if you’re worried about skin staining
- Dont exfoliate the day of dyeing and the skin stain will come up easier
- use a cotton bud lightly dipped in skin salve/Vaseline to scrub up skin stain rather than washing it away to avoid early fading on brow hairs- even just applying a bit to brows and leaving it on for a while before wiping it away can really get it off much easier AND avoid irritating the skin
- wipe away areas you want to be lighter half way through your dyeing process (Ex: if you want the inner part of the brow to be lighter than the tail, wipe away some dye on the inner part and leave more to develop on the tail)
- You can reapply dye if you feel it didn’t tint enough in one session. Just leave any you didn’t use up on the counter and only discard extra after you’re satisfied with the color payoff (don’t save dye for another day, just go ahead and reapply right after taking off the first application if you feel you want more color)

review_title: Great Mask! A Lot of Product!
review_text:
These are great masks! There seems to be a lot of product on the masks, which I wasn’t sure I’d like at first. But, after using a few of them, it really seems like your face is getting the extra benefit of the extra product. With most sheet masks, there’s product on them, but once they sit on your face and you remove the mask, there’s only a little residue left, that you rub into your skin. With these masks, it seems like there was a lot left after. So, I rubbed it into my face after. With all the excess product, I feel like my skin is getting mote of the benefits. You can feel the bubbling, which feels interesting but in a good way!

The only weird thing I found was, with most sheet masks, you apply the mask, let it sit for the appropriate time, remove the mask, rub in any excess product left over, and you’re done. With these masks, however, the instructions say to re-wash your face after removing the mask. It says, “Apply the mask to face after cleaning. Remove it after 15-20 minutes. Re-clean skin until it is completely absorbed.” That makes zero sense to me. “Re-clean skin until it is completely absorbed” 🤷‍♀️ If you’re washing your face after removing the mask, the product won’t be absorbed, it will be washed off. So that makes no sense. I’m not sure what that’s about. So, I would leave the mask on for the 15-20 min, remove the mask, rub in the excess product for a minute, then rinse off my face.

I love that you get 10 masks! A lot of facial sheet masks you only get one or you get 10 but at a higher cost. So, I love you get 10 of these, and that they didn’t skimp at all on the product on the masks! I definitely recommend these!

review_text:
First of all, my hair is very long and I'm 56 so it is aging. It has gotten coarser, dryer, and duller as I've gotten older so what I need from a conditioner may be different than someone with a different type of hair. I found that this conditioner took about three days of use before it actually made my hair start to feel soft, but even after some time, it wasn't as soft as some other conditioners can make it. On the bright side, comb out was easier with this than some other conditioners. It also didn't weigh my hair down or flatten out the natural waves. It left my hair bouncy and full of body. However, it also didn't do much for shine enhancement or split ends/repair as far as I could tell.

The scent on this conditioner is very herb-like (as you'd expect) and not especially strong which I prefer in a conditioner as I don't like the scent lingering in my hair. It is fairly thick and a smaller amount goes a long way. I think the claims about "hydrating" are sound, but my hair isn't super dry or brittle (though it is a bit dry), but there are other qualities (softening, shine enhancement) that I wasn't satisfied with.

review_text: I deliberately ordered Northern Lights silver holo topper after reading about how thinly scattered the holo bits are.  When I do galaxy nails, I use 2 or 3 of the scattered holo toppers, layered with a super thick, quick drying top coat, so it gives depth and dimension to my nails, and for the stars that appear farthest away, I prefer a micro-micro glitter that is not densely packed, and apply those coats in reverse, with the  smallest/thinnest one going last.  I also prefer holo toppers that don't have colored glitter added, and this Northern Lights formula is perfect for me, with just the standard silver holo particles and no bonus colors added.  I generally don't like gold color items, but am going to get the gold version of Northern Lights too, because this particular holo topper is very impressive.  The way I look at it, the more intensely packed toppers don't look like a galaxy.  They can be used to create milky way looking area, but this topper makes deep space look better.  It's kind of difficult to explain making galaxy nails to a non nail person, which is who I'm aimed at.  Those, and the newbies, are my intended readers. So I hope this made sense.  But I love this stuff!

The body wash arrives in its own logo cardboard box. Suitable for gift giving.

The bottle itself is a pump bottle, with a beautiful label and Silver colored accent on the pump. It really is pretty.

review_text:
I used the small, black five star g-whiz twice in 48 hours. I rinsed the blades off with tap water. Next morning, the blades had rust on them. I got a full refund by Amazon since I bought it directly from them. End of story.

Wahl customer support, I want to buy and like your products, but now I've got to ask which of your products do not have this problem. I just want a cordless battery powered trimmer that won't rust. As sales and business owners, it really doesn't make economic sense to sell something with metal in it guaranteed to rust as soon as it hits water, since people are going to do a 180 and get a refund.

Maybe the metal does have the benefit of being easier to machine and result in higher quality blades, but it's really not an option to have easily oxidized metal in a product that gets washed frequently.

I'm open to buying Wahl trimmers again, but I need recommendations for which models won't have fundamental engineering design flaws. I'll spend the money, just tell me what actually works.

P.S. the trimmer works fine otherwise. Maybe a little wimpy in terms of power output, but no hair pulling. Pretty noisy, but who cares. Just lubricate it properly. It's smaller than the Remington MB4900, but the blade width is almost as long. It's lightweight and very small, so I guess if you have gigantic man-hands it might not offer the best ergonomics. I actually prefer non-permanent batteries, so that was a plus for me. The trimmer heads aren't easily removable for cleaning. I don't think the body is very waterproof (aside from the obvious aforementioned blade rusting), so be wary about using it in the shower.

review_title: Isopropyl-based hand sanitizer that meets both CDC & WHO guidelines
review_text:
Much of the hand sanitizer we have been using is ETHYL alcohol (ethanol) based. THIS sanitizer is ISOPROPYL alcohol based. Note that historically most hand sanitizer has been based on isopropyl alcohol whereas ethanol has been used in things like alcohol that you drink of as a gasoline additive for oxygenated fuels (for environmental purposes) as well as other purposes. Isopropyl has been used in hand sanitizer and "rubbing alcohol" among other things. Both are now approved for use in hand sanitizer. Ethynol-based sanitzers are becoming much more common due to high demand and supply constraints on Isopropyl-based sanitizers.

The interesting thing is that the CDC and WHO have different guidelines for hand sanitizer effectiveness for these two types of alcohol:
CDC: Ethyl - at least 60%, Isopropyl - at least 70%
WHO: Ethyl - at least 80%, Isopropyl - at least 75%
You can see that it is interesting that the CDC recommends higher concentrations of Isopropyl whereas WHO recommends higher concentrations of Ethyl. Curious. Rather than dig into too many details on the difference, the easiest thing is to find a way to meet both...

The most common ethyl alcohol hand sanitizers that we have been getting (and the most common out there) are 70% -- which exceeds CDC 60% threshold, but is below the 80% WHO threshold.

THIS SANITIZER has an ISOPROPYL concentration of 75% which exceeds the CDC 70% threshold and meets the WHO 75% threshold.

Clearly these thresholds are not hard limits as indicated by the difference of opinion between CDC and WHO, but it is mildly comforting to meet both recommendations if you can do so with no downside or extra expense.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Easily squeezes out of bottle in controlled amount as a gel
* Rubs in easily and absorbs within less than a minute to leave no noticeable residue or tackiness on your hands
* Aloe helps to keep your hands moist, fighting the drying effects of the alcohol
* Small bottles are easy to take in car, backpack, purse, etc.
* Scent is minor and dissipates quickly (we're not using this for its smell after all)

SUMMARY:
A cost effective way to keep you hands sanitized when you can't use soap & water. Meets both CDC and WHO guidelines for effective hand sanitizer formulations.

review_title: just like mousse or shaving cream, but is a soap for body
review_text:
The bottle and texture is very much like a hair mousse or shaving cream, but is a wash for the body. Instead of a pump or squeeze bottle, this comes out though as pressure aerosol - also just like a mousse or shaving cream. The ingredients necessary to make this happen are Butane and Propane. They are aerosol propellents. If you have ever used mousse, hair spray, various perfumes/body sprays, air fresheners, aerosol deodorants, or shaving cream,etc.. then you are already familiar with these ingredients. They are generally recognized as safe, and are used in small, diluted quantities in skin care. Fun fact, "These ingredients are used in cosmetics and personal care products as a replacements for chlorofluorocarbons, or CFC propellants, some of which have been shown to have negative effects on the environment". I'm not a big fan of slathering my body with butane, propane, or isobutane, but I understand their use in this type of medium. So it's up to you to decide.

This company does have non aerosol body wash available too..

The resulting foamy wash comes out thick, it is creamy. Because it reminds me so much of a shaving cream, that it what I have been using it for. Then whatever is left over I use on rest of body. Is pleasant smelling enough to me but it isn't quite a pure aromatherapy experience for me. Clearly it uses a variety of essential oils- rosemary, orange, eucalyptus, peppermint, limonene. However, for whatever reason, it contains "parfum (fragrance)" as an added ingredient. As well as Alpha-Isomethyl Ionone, another synthetic fragrance ingredient. Is there not enough naturally occurring scent from the use of essential oils? I think the added synthetic fragrance is redundant and takes away from the olfactory experience.

As an actual wash, it is fine.
3 stars-- this is just a middle of the road rating. I am not in love. The experience is underwhelming. I am much too quickly going through the container. Aromatherapy experience is a little off as I pick up on something other than essential oils. Otherwise the cleansing action is fine. But.. I likely won't repurchase.

I think if I really want a foam wash, I will just use another body wash or make my own wash and pour into a foaming soap dispenser.

review_text:
I normally stick to one brand for my skin care routine. But, I have wanted to try a Vitamin C serum, (without sticker shock of my normal brand).
—I’m using this product for middle age skin- collagen loss, wrinkles and uneven skin (rough patches).
—My skin facial skin is dry. Very little oil production.
—I’m new to Vitamin C serums. I began using this product daily. It dried out/irritated my skin. I cut back to 2-3x/week (after a skin a little break). The dryness and irritation went away.
—For those accustomed to Vitamin C serums- this might not be an issue.
—I also followed the recommendations to refrigerate after opening to prolong longevity (Vitamin C is very unstable in liquid form)
—I’m into Naturopathy and clean skin scare products. There were no questionable ingredients on the box label (via EWG SkinDeep website).
—I’ve researched different forms of Vitamin C: serums and powders with and without feurlic acid to understand what to look for in a Vitamin C serum.
Pro’s
EWG SkinDeep database check came back Good. (ingredient list label is difficult to read. One ingredient wasn’t recognized in EWG)
Dark glass bottle with screw on lid. Comes with dropper that also screws onto bottle.
Clear and semi-watery serum (Vitamin C serum should be clear, not yellow, brown or cloudy). No oiliness....very liquidity.
Ample size- 1.01 fluid ounces
Easy to apply- 2-3 drops is sufficient
Sinks into skin quickly
Improvement of rough patches (face feels smoother)- thinking of trying this on back of hands.
Works with my current skincare products (facial wash, toner, facial oil, mask 2x/week)
Solution has not turned brown or discolored (kept refrigeration)
My skin feels tighter (firmness)

Cons:
A slight odor, I can’t place
Not a significant difference in wrinkle improvement (50- beginning of smile lines, chin and forehead wrinkles).
No feurlic acid (this has been shown to work synergistically with Vitamin C)
Lasts 3 months and needs refrigeration (expiration date is on box)...since very little is needed and use is 2-3x/week- I expect it will expire before all product is used. Would love to see this in powder form for longevity.

Conclusion: A lot of thought was put into formulating and, bottling this product. If opting for “serum” over “powdered” Vitamin C- this is a good option. I’m always hesitant to try products that are not EWG Verified. But, the ingredients listed, received a good score on EWG SkinDeep Database. It just takes a little more time to to investigate each ingredient.

review_text:
This comes with an outer product box. The tube is a squeeze tube that has a cap that flips open and closed.

The box says that this is “for dry to normal skin with light to moderate acne.” It says, “sulfur-enhanced benzoyl peroxide penetrates deeply to loosen pore-clogging debris and hardened oils while killing bacteria and soothing inflammation. This has 5% benzoyl peroxide in it as the active ingredient and 3% sulfur as an inactive ingredient to fight acne. I really liked that it listed the percentage of each in the product.

This is a medium consistency cream. It glides onto the skin easily, absorbs quickly, and doesn’t leave any stickiness or residue. It says to apply this sparingly to affected areas once or twice daily as needed. It says that dryness and light peeling may occur during the first few weeks of usage. I used this as instructed, sparingly on affected areas, and chose to sometimes use it twice a day and sometimes only once a day. If I was going out and wearing makeup, I didn’t apply this in the morning, only at night. If I wasn’t going to be wearing makeup and was staying home, then I applied it twice a day (morning and night). I don’t have sensitive skin. I have normal to dry skin, with some areas extremely dry. Usually when I use heavy duty acne fighting products, I get a lot of dryness in the area. I did have slight dryness in the areas I used this if I used it twice a day for a few days in a row. Like one time, I used this twice a day for 4 days in a row. I got a little bit of dryness in the areas I used it in, but after not using this product and applying a good moisturizer morning and night on the area for 2 days, the dryness was gone. After that, I didn’t use this twice a day for more than 3 days in a row. Once I started making sure to do that, I didn’t experience any more dryness.

I really liked the results with this! It really helped my breakouts go away a lot quicker than they do on their own or with other products I’ve used in the past. I also felt this helped keep breakouts away because I usually suffer from hormonal breakouts, but I started using this in those areas before I would usually get a hormonal breakout, and I didn’t get one! So, while this is on the pricier end for me, it’s definitely something I’ll purchase when I run out! And it’s definitely something I recommend if you’re suffering from breakouts!

review_title: Thank G-d, a company that understands that scents are bad
review_text:
OK, so I have used ampules for many years, of various kinds, since I started the Korean skin care routine. I cannot speak to the power of the ingredients here, because generally these things take time to show results. But I did like the creamy feel and the way this felt on my skin. I've been curious about trying pro-biotics for some time, and the other ingredients intrigued me, but only time will tell if this changes anything at all. If you are buying this, you are more or less in the same boat. What I DEFINITELY appreciate is that this is scent free. So many products feel the need to load up on supposedly "mild" fragrance. Well, NEWS FLASH! A "mild" scent can quickly become overwhelming when mixed with other products as you do in the Korean method. Secondly, people who are sensitive to scents (triggers migraines) are more common than you might think. Having a perfume in a face product serves no purpose at all, and I am grateful that this company understands.

The label on the bottle is completely in Korean, which means you can't tell what is inside. I had to come here to see. That is a small thing, and did not effect my opinion of the product.

With gel polish, you have to let the polish set into the design for about 20 seconds, scrap, let set another 20 seconds, then pick up the design. review_title: Seems to be the real deal
review_text:
Rosehip oil is in my top 5 favorite oils to use on my skin and nails, top 10 for my hair. Unfortunately, buying non food grade oils always seems to be a bit of a gamble as there aren't any regulations or standards in place to ensure a product is what it claims to be. Except for meeting the qualifications to be labeled organic.

I've tried several different brands and I do believe the Tropical Holistic brand of Rosehip Seed oil is 100% rosehip seed oil and doesn't contain any other oils and isn't diluted. I'm basing that assessment on good results and comparison with previous brands.

This oil had a light almost nutty scent, it was almost odorless, but not quite. it was a pale amber color, and low to medium viscosity.

Rosehip oil is one of the "oilier" beauty oils. What I mean is, it tends to take it a but longer to be absorbed into the skin than a dry oil. So, I like to use this after my evening shower as a body oil. I think this would make a great massage oil, as well. It's a little too thick to use it as part of my morning skin routine, but I have used it on the ends of my hair in the mornings with good results. It really helps tame the frizz and flyaways on humid days, but it is a little heavy for everyday use.

This is priced a little higher than other options for sale on Amazon, but I think it's worth the price. I feel confident that I'm actually getting the product that's promised, and it's organic. Personally, I think this is a great item to add to your collection of beauty products.

review_title: It definitely helps correct skin tone differences & does smooth pores in SOME areas.
review_text:
I got this in Nude. I have some areas in my face that have some sun damage, some broken capillaries, and some enlarged pores. The only thing that I've found that covers these completely is concealer for the first two, only two primers do the job on the pores that I've found. I figured this might give me some additional coverage due to the nude tint so maybe I could skip the concealer and just go with foundation for coverage. I was also hoping it would be another primer that would blur/fill the pores and not just "disappear" after foundation gets applied.

I was actually impressed by the tone correction I got from this. It's not a concealer (obviously), so I wasn't expecting full coverage. I was just looking for a muting of the redness & the sun spots so I could maybe skip the concealer. It did exactly that. It provided a veil of nude tint that made my areas of sun damage and sun spots (yeah, they're freckles) almost disappear. The redness was muted somewhat. Enough that I when I skipped the concealer I was pretty happy with the result I got from just this product under my foundation. That being said, it doesn't play well with every foundation. I noticed that it doesn't seem to work as well with my dewy/hydrating foundations. That may just be a "me thing", but I thought I'd throw it out there for consideration.

So, this leads to the pore filling/smoothing. It does smooth out some areas with pores and it does continue to do that after the foundations is applied.....in some areas. Which seem to be in the areas that don't move a lot. So on my face, I have enlarged pores on the side of my nose in the nostril area and down toward my mouth, on my chin, and on my forehead in the center. Now, everyone's face moves but we don't all emote with our faces in the same areas. I tend to have a very expressive mouth and I arch one eyebrow a lot. I don't furrow or wrinkle my forehead much. The primer didn't hold up on my chin or around the nostrils and down toward my mouth. The center of the forehead held up perfectly.
So, while I like this primer for the tone correction, I need something that smooths my pores in all areas of my face. If you're just looking for a good primer to even out your skin tone or provide some base color correction I would absolutely recommend this one. The pore thing....I think that's going to be something that depends on the person. This definitely has a place in my makeup routine. I can use it in the areas where I need the tone correction and use something else for my problem pore areas. It's perfect for my light makeup days and I'm going to try it with just some light powder on my next "no makeup" makeup day.

review_text:
A small amount of this lathers and cleans well. Rinses away easily, doesn't seem to dry my scalp or leave my hair unruly.

The scent is distinctly fruity, in keeping with the muscat (grape) theme, sweet but not cloying, with some citrus. I like it.

250ml is about 8-1/2 fluid ounces, so don't expect a large container.

The description says this has no sulfates, but the first ingredient is one. Sodium laureth sulfate, or SLES, isn't SLS, which some are trying to avoid, but it's still a sulfate, a milder one, that a few may find to be an irritant.

Cocamidopropyl betaine was once believed to be an allergen, but it turned out it was impurities from the manufacturing process, hopefully avoided here.

Ingredients (with corrected spellings): Sodium laureth sulfate, cocamidopropyl betaine, glycol distearate, cocodiethanolamide, trimethylcetylammonium chloride, polyquaternium-16, keratin, sodium benzoate, fragrance, citric acid.

review_title: Loaded with hydration & plant extracts that my skin NEEDS during the winter months!!
review_text: These masks have become a favorite this fall and winter when my skin needs an extra dose of hydration.  I've just turned 50 and it's a constant battle to keep my skin hydrated just due to the aging process.  When you add in cold, dry air outside and hot, dry air inside it just makes it so much more difficult.  I've been adding masks to my skincare routine this winter and they've made a huge difference.  I try to do at LEAST one a week, but as it gets colder I've been using them every few days.  I'll use them at night after I've cleansed and used my prescription skincare and then I'll follow up with my nightly routine.  I love all of the plant extracts loaded into this one along with the niacinamide and hyaluronic acid.  One thing to keep in mind though is that if you're using this (or anything with hyaluronic acid, really) and you're in a dry climate you need to make sure you provide additional moisture for the HA to bind to.  It's why I use this one at night since I keep a humidifier running on my bedside table that pumps that moisture into the air.  In addition to the hydration it also does a great job of noticeably minimizing the appearance of some of larger pores on my face which of course makes my skin look firmer and smoother.

I'm 49 with decent skin aside from some minor redness/capillaries near my nose and a couple dark spots here and there.

I bought this for a quick 'more coverage than powder' solution for when I have last minute zoom calls for work.

While definitely good for the purpose I use it for, the coverage is moderate at best. Goes on well and stays on fairly well. Evens out most of my skin tone, aside from a couple dark spots. Definitely works better over a primer than just over moisturizer, which isn't a huge issue for me. And patting it on, as the instructions state versus swirling it on does result in a fuller coverage and nicer finish.

While in person it wasn't as blurred and flawless as a full makeup, it definitely was suitable for video calls or more casual days.

I didn't notice any transfer, but I did have to touchup my chin and nose after a few hours, which was very easy to do (no problem with old over fresh not blending well)

If feels very soft and light on my skin. Very comfortable. I almost forgot to take it off at the end of the day I first wore it, as it felt very natural.

For my purposes, this worked exactly as I hoped. I would definitely consider buying it again, although it is not a holy grail replacement for my liquid foundation.

review_title: Minty & Cooling, Heavy & Doesn’t Absorb Well, Agitates My Sensitive Skin-Some Good Ingredients
review_text:
﻿I’m in my 50’s and have dry, sensitive skin and also have some contact allergies. This Murad Hydration Intense Recovery Cream is pale green and has a nice, light spearmint scent that may be from mint oils, such as Mentha Viridis Leaf Oil and Mentha Arvensis Leaf Oil, as chemical fragrance isn’t listed. This cream has an unusual balmy texture that feels slippery and silky. It oddly feels like it just sits on top of my dry skin rather being absorbed. It’s not greasy, but it feels heavy like a barrier cream. I’m not crazy about that feel. I do like that it’s thick and has somewhat of a firming feel.

I’d be okay with the texture at night (not for daytime), but this cream imparts a strong cooling sensation (possibly from mint oil as this is alcohol free) that doesn’t feel pleasing to me. Instead of feeling soothing and calming, it feels stimulating and kind of agitating. My skin gets itchy and prickly, so I’ve had to wash it off as my skin feels uncomfortable and like it might blister or get a rash (though it hasn’t in the short time I’ve left it on). It feels better rubbed on my arm, so maybe it’s good for other skin types.

I can’t gauge how well this hydrates as I had to discontinue use. It has some good stuff like apple fruit extract (scavenges free radicals) and algae (antioxidant and hydration). It also has moisturizing and/or soothing ingredients, such as glycerin, vitamin E, butylene glycol, macadamia nut oil and shea butter. However, it also has known sensitizers, such as spearmint and mint oils, that get “poor” ratings by Paula’s Choice. This generally seems like a quality cream, but it feels heavy and irritating to my sensitive skin. 3.5 stars.

review_text:
After going over the ingredients in these products, the only two I would feel even remotely safe using would be this shampoo and conditioner. As a hair stylist, you do not want to use a product that contains formaldehyde and apply heat to it. You certainly do not want to use it every 6 weeks, as it's harmful to your health. It can cause breathing issues among other things. It's very hard to believe that I even saw actual formaldehyde on the back of this product, and so high up in the ingredients list.
Even hair stylist must wear protective gear, such as gloves, aprons, masks, and be trained how to safely work with this hazardous chemical. Salons must have adequate ventilation and follow strict protocols regarding blow dryer temperatures and monitor formaldehyde levels at all times when they provide Keratin Treatments containing formaldehyde because of the immediate and long term health dangers.This is something you cannot possibly do at home.
Also, the pretreatment that you add to the shampoo is extremely strong and stripping to your hair. When they say add just a little, no one knows what that means. That particular product, or the two main ingredients, should only be a small percentage of the product you're adding it to. I don't think you can mix this properly at home without causing damage to your hair and/or your skin.
I "might" use the shampoo and conditioner, but I will not touch the pre-treatment nor will I touch the DIY home keratin treatment. Over the course of a few treatments, I can see this product going really awry for some people. They will end up with damaged hair and possibly other problems. It is not safe. I absolutely would not recommend it!

review_text:
I have extremely fine hair and I didn't use the hair tie to hold the ponytail together, only to wrap around the ponytail and the elastic came out of 1 of the 4 sides of the metal crimp bead holding it together.
I didn't expect them to be as good as the ones in the 70s & 80s (**considering there are STILL several around my parents house that have the elastic in tact, but 1 or more of the balls are broken) but I did expect to be able to use them wo breaking them.
To be fair, it's been a very long time since I've used a hair tie like this and I break the first clear elastic I use to put in a ponytail at least every other morning, so I don't know if I was just pulling too hard or if this one had a faulty crimp. They are cute. I ended up with some triplets and singles, but that was not important to me and if I still had little girl in hair bows, would have bought 2 of these and any combo of a second package would most likely pair up the colors if that is important to someone. I wouldn't order assorted colors of anything I wanted specific colors for wo realizing I was taking a chance of getting the mix I wanted, but I did think I was getting 6 matching pair of these and I didn't.

I will pinch the center crimp bead on the rest of these w pliers and assume I was being too hard on them. I will use another week and update the review only if the others break.
I don't remember these being so relatively expensive as far as hair ties go, but I have zero reference point.
I purchased them to put around the ponytail of my bun and I am trying to attach the back of a bandana to the little balls. These worked alright, but I am going to have to end up going with a bungie cord that has a ball on it. I say that only to provide the grain of salt one should probably take with the review.

These are pricey to me, but very cute and visually identical to the bubble balls of the 70's I would never use this tie to hold hair, but to embellish. Clearly 6 matching pair are not necessarily the case in assorted but mostly they were. If it is this specific look you are going for, these are what I remember. In case it's the design, use pliers to squeeze the metal crimp in the center of each one until it's flat, but don't do it so much that you cut the elastic and be gentle putting them in.

review_text:
I like to try different kinds of lotions and self care products because it's fun and relaxing. I was offered this Isavera Anti-Cellulite Cream and though I'm always skeptical of "anti this or that" creams I still like to see if they're any good as a lotion. At time of review a bottle runs $29.99, which to me is on the pricier end of similar sized bottles....

The lotion has a lot of really great things in it to do what it says (anti cellulite), you have retinol, eucalyptus, aloe, citrus, chamomile. Now things like retinol and citrus are acidic and can remove layers of dead skin which will help improve look. Things like eucalyptus stimulates blood flow which could help reduce the look of cellulite however temporarily. Chamomile and aloe will help soothe the skin. All great things. Now the directions say massage the lotion in for several minutes. Again this is going to stimulate blood flow in the area and help REDUCE the look of cellulite. So it's not going to go away, lets be honest here. However, the lotion itself is VERY nice, feels cooling and soothing- moisturizes nicely without being too oily or sticky and a great thing to do to relax in the morning and at night (as they recommend application 2x daily). I think it's a great lotion but I am a little on the fence about whether the price is too high. You be the judge there.

﻿Ogana Cell Bio Actiome Recovery Cream is a wonderful cream for my dry, sensitive skin. This is a thick, heavy, white cream with very subtle fragrance (last ingredient). This cream feels rich, but my dry skin doesn’t look greasy and my skin is dry enough that I’ve used this during the day. Still, it’s heavy and I prefer it as a night cream. It makes my skin feel calm, supple and so hydrated that it minimizes my fine lines.

When I first applied this cream, it felt kind of like a barrier cream. While I love rich creams, I dislike creams that sit heavy on top of my skin as it feels annoying to me like my skin can’t breathe. But this Ogana Cell cream feels good as it turns out it absorbs well and feels like it only leaves just a light, protective layer that’s breathable on my skin. It’s probably just the feel of the occlusive dimethicone. This cream feels good and isn’t too heavy for me.

This cream is perfect for times my face gets irritated or agitated as it feels extra gentle and calming. I also used a little of this cream on the back of my hands when they feel dry and get red as this cream is soothing and makes them feel better. My eyebrows have faded as I've aged but their shape is still good, so I just need something to darken them up a bit. I usually use a tinted gel because I sometimes get carried away with pencils, which makes my brows look huge & angry. Also, I have to set the pencil with a clear gel, anyway, so a tinted gel saves me a step. I've recently found a pencil that I liked through either Ipsy or Birchbox & this pencil looked similar, so I decided to give it a try.

It has a pencil with an angled tip on one end & the other end has a spoolie. The pencil can be advanced or retracted with a twist of the shaft. It seems to be well-made but, at first, I couldn't get the pencil to draw. It was so hard & dry that nothing would come off. It took several minutes of rubbing it on the back of my hand before I finally got a faint line of color. I had to keep going for several more minutes before I could consistently get color to come off the pencil.

Once I tried it on my brows, I was pleasantly surprised. The color, Dark Brown, is good for me but I would call it more of a medium brown. I have dark brown, almost black, hair but I feel like if I match my brows to my hair, they look too harsh, so I like to keep them softer, which makes this color perfect for me.

Overall, I do like this pencil but it still seems a little too dry, even after several uses. It could be a fluke with just this particular pencil. I'd be willing to purchase another as long as the price was reasonable.

product_title: GERMAINE DE CAPUCCINI - Timexpert SRNS Repair Night Progress Serum - Advanced Anti-Ageing Booster with an Innovative Active Ingredient That Increases 8 Times the Power of Absorption - 1.7 oz
details_json: {"Brand": "Germaine de Capuccini", "Item Form": "Lotion", "Unit Count": "1.70 Fl Oz", "Number of Items": "1", "Skin Type": "All", "Product Dimensions": "1.57 x 1.97 x 5.12 inches; 1.7 Ounces", "Item model number": "480777"}
review_title: Nope...much better options out there that actually work for sooo much less than this.
review_text:
Overall, the product is okay. It glides onto the skin nicely. It feels silky smooth (thanks to the silicones in it). But, my skin doesn’t feel extra hydrated, I haven’t noticed any difference after using it for a month, let alone 7 days. I don’t like rating things based on price, but when it comes to something at this price point, I feel like it’s going to play a part in the decision, at least for me it would. And for me, the ingredients and effects resulting from this product just aren’t there to justify this price point. Honestly, even if it was way cheaper (like $20), I still wouldn’t purchase it. There’s so many great skincare products out there that are waaaaaay cheaper that I’ve actually seen results from. So, I can’t recommend this.

I wanted to love this.....

A serum for $171 (at the time of writing this review), I figured this had to have some pretty special stuff in it. I mean, it must have some kind of magic potion in it that reverses time and makes me look like I’m 20 years old again. Right? I mean, it’s gotta have something pretty darn special in it to price it so high and expect people to pay it. Plus, it’s not even from a brand I had ever heard anything about, so it wasn’t just some name brand that was what would hike the price up...You know, how some companies just feel like since their brand is well known and popular that they can slap their name on their products and it doesn’t matter if there’s nothing in them or about them that would account for the price other than the brand name?! Yeah, well as far as I know this isn’t a well known, or even known brand, so that’s definitely not the reason for the high price. So that means there has to be something in it that makes it worth a higher price. And it has to be something amazing to make it worth a price as high as $171 for 1.7 oz of product! Right?! Unfortunately, that does not seem to be the case.

The info for this product on the Amazon product page is seriously LACKING! On the top of the product page where there’s usually some bullet points with info, there’s nothing. You scroll down a little and there’s a small paragraph. It claims to “rejuvenate your skin in 7 days.” That’s a HUGE claim! Most skin care product I use and have tried usually say to use consistently for a month or so before you’ll see results. So, to claim to see results in 7 days is huge. Looking at this product on the company’s website, it states that clinical tests were done “under dermatological control on 29 volunteers aged between 35 and 60, including sensitive skin.” It states that 81% had “skin more radiant, luminous and revitalised ,” 81% had “visibly rejuvenated skin,” and “in 1 month all the signs of aging are visibly corrected.” Again, some HUGE claims, but it seems 81% is the lucky number 🤨

The ingredients weren’t included on the product page. All it says is, “The new anti-ageing serum includes an innovative active ingredient that multiplies by 8 the power of absorption(2) of your skin, making the serum penetrate deeper.” Ummmm....what?! I don’t know about you, but that description is not helpful in any way! I’m not even totally sure I get what it’s trying to say. It includes an innovative active ingredient....why not say what that innovative active ingredient is? This innovative active ingredient multiplies by 8 the power of absorption of your skin. What on earth is that supposed to mean? “...multiplies by 8 the power of absorption of your skin...” I take it to mean that this ingredient multiplies the absorption of your skin by the power of 8, so 8 times. Looking at the company’s website and the info for this product on there, most of it says the same things but some parts are said differently, which makes it seem clearer, at least to me. It states, “...includes an innovative active ingredient that increases 8 times the power of absorption(2) of your skin making the serum penetrate deeper...” So, that definitely makes me think it’s saying it increases absorption of your skin 8 times. But, it just would be nice if they stated that in a way that was a little clearer.

The paragraph description on the product page also says that the innovative active ingredient that increases the absorption power of your skin 8 times makes “the serum penetrate deeper and activate the capacity of self-protection during the day and unfold all its power of regeneration by night, working in a synchronized way and thus achieving more visible results in less time.” It does state you use the serum morning and night. But, I wondered how the heck the serum would know to work differently in the day than it does at night. How would it know to activate self-protection during the day and start regenerating at night? It states that, “At night, when you sleep and while your skin is more receptive, it repairs damage, reactivates cellular regeneration and rejuvenates your skin. By day it increases the resistance of cells to oxidative stress and protects the skin defending it against external aggression.” Again, I don’t really see how it would know to do something different at night than it does during the day? But, I’m not a scientist so it could just be beyond my understanding!

It sure would be nice to know what they believe is this innovative ingredient, because looking at the Amazon product page it doesn’t mention much, let alone what this innovative ingredient is. Looking at the product on the company’s website it states “NEW AND REVOLUTIONARY FORMULA. 22 ACTIVE INGREDIENTS.” It goes on to state that the serum incorporates “Glyco 8-Power biomolecules that generate small vesicles that trap inside them the active ingredients of the formula. Their great affinity for the lipids of the skin make them penetrate easily, liberating the content inside, increasing by 8 the capacity of absorption and multiplying the benefits of the serum on your skin.” I have no clue what “glyco 8-power biomolecules” are and doing a search on Google doesn’t explain it either. All that shows up is this serum. I’m not sure if the “innovative ingredient” is supposed to be the “glyco 8-power biomolecules?”

INGREDIENTS
Let’s take a look at this products ingredients...

Antioxidant Ingredients: Tocopherol (Vitamin E), Ascorbyl Tetraisopalmitate, Polygonum Cuspidatum Root Extract, Scutellaria Baicalensis Root Extract, Centella Asiatica Extract, Rosmarinus Officinalis (Rosemary) Leaf Extract, Chamomilla Recutita (Matricaria) Flower Extract, Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract, Tocopheryl Acetate (Vitamin E)

Cell-Communicating Ingredient: Retinyl Palmitate (Vitamin A)

Skin Brightening Ingredients: Ascorbyl Tetraisopalmitate, Glycyrrhiza Glabra (Licorice) Root Extract

Skin-Identical Ingredients: Glycerin, Squalane, Sodium Hyaluronate, Ceramide 3

Soothing Ingredients: Scutellaria Baicalensis Root Extract, Centella Asiatica Extract, Rosmarinus Officinalis (Rosemary) Leaf Extract, Glycyrrhiza Glabra (Licorice) Root Extract, Chamomilla Recutita (Matricaria) Flower Extract, Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract, Panthenol

Antimicrobial/Antibacterial Ingredients: Scutellaria Baicalensis Root Extract, Rosmarinus Officinalis (Rosemary) Leaf Extract, Alcohol, O-Cymen-5-Ol

Moisturizer/Humectant Ingredients: Glycerin, Pentylene Glycol, Ethoxydiglycol, Caprylyl Glycol, Butylene Glycol, Dimethiconol, Hydrolyzed Hyaluronic Acid, Soluble Collagen, Scutellaria Baicalensis Root Extract, Centella Asiatica Extract, Prunus Persica (Peach) Kernel Extract, Sodium Hyaluronate, Panthenol, Sorbitol

Perfuming: Ethoxydiglycol, Fragrance

Preservative: Potassium Sorbate, Phenoxyethanol, O-Cymen-5-Ol

Theres a total of 57 ingredients.

Theres 3 ingredients that I consider great (superstar) ingredients - glycerin, licorice root extract, and Camellia Sinensis Leaf Extract.

There’s 18 ingredients that I consider to be good - sunflower seed oil, hydrogenated lecithin, bifida ferment lysate, milk protein, squalane, vitamin E, Shea butter extract, hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid, vitamin c, soluble collagen, Polygonum cuspidatum root extract, scutellaria baicalensis root extract, centella asiatica extract, Lupinus Albus Seed Extract, rosemary leaf extract, sodium hyaluronate, retinyl palmitate, and Panthenol.

Even though there’s a total of 21 great and good ingredients, that is less than half of the ingredients. In a product as high priced as this, I expect a lot more great (superstar) type ingredients. To get me to pay $171 (at the time of writing this review) for a skincare product, it needs to have way more than 3 ingredients that I consider superstar ingredients.

Plus, there’s 4 different silicones and alcohol in this product, which is pretty unacceptable for a skincare product at this price point.

There’s also fragrance in it. It’s the last ingredient. It has a very faint smell. I can’t quite place it. Kind of perfume scented, but very faint.

In the end, I just don’t see where they come up with the price point for this. I feel that way about a lot of the so-called “big name brand” products, where just because they’re a well-known brand, they feel it justifies slapping a bigger price on it, even when the ingredients and/or results don’t seem to justify it. But, this brand isn’t even a known brand, unless you’re a small spa or boutique as far as I can tell. So, that definitely doesn’t justify the price (not that I think it would even if it was a well known brand). But, the ingredients also don’t justify the price. There isn’t enough superstar type ingredients in this to justify the price. There’s a bunch of basic good ingredients, and a few superstar, and then some not great ingredients like fragrance, alcohol, and different silicones. I find that unacceptable when you’re trying to charge this much. Not to mention, they claim results occur in 7 days. I used this for a month and didn’t see any results at all. I don’t even feel like it provides much hydration. It just feels silky smooth on the skin...thanks to the silicones. So, I don’t recommend this.

review_title: Massage roller=good quality. Gua Sha=average quality.
review_text:
The quality of the components of the set is not equal. Of the two pieces in this set, the massage roller clearly outshines the gua sha. The massage roller has rich, dark green aventurine/jade stone rollers and center handle. The stones are not highly polished, but there is a natural feel to the jade stones. The metal arms/axles have a metal collar ring where it meets the stone rollers. It may be mostly cosmetic, but it's an attractive visual element. Also, at this juncture is the plastic grommet that better quality massage rollers possess. These grommets act as a bearing for a quiet and smoother rolling action. Perhaps just as important, it serves to protect the stone and metal prong from eroding due to abrasive interaction. The handle seems to be composed of aventurine/jade, too and not plastic/resin material. Very high marks for the massage roller.
The gua sha, with a lighter green hue than the massage roller, follows the thinner, flattened design. It's not very polished, with more of a natural stone feel. While this is subject to personal preference, less polish tends to result in less of a glossy appearance, and a surface that is not as smooth. Perhaps as a consequence of this level of polishing, nicks and rough textures are more readily apparent. Such is the case in the gua sha I received. There's a number of nick, pock marks and small scratches on the stone surface. Due to the thin nature of the gua sha, there is less of a gentle rounding of the edges, too. This results in more of a definite edging on the contour of the gua sha (sort of similar to a coin edge). I like the quality of the aventurine/jade stone, but feels it doesn't match the quality of manufacture exhibited by the massage roller.
The colors of the pieces are not really in sync. Individually, they are nice examples of their respective massage types. The massage roller has a high quality look and feel, the gua sha falls in the average quality realm.
Based on these observations and considerations, this set receives a 4.0 - 4.25 star rating.

review_title: Thought this was amazing, but now only like it..read UPDATE at bottom of review
review_text:
I’d been using the Sol De Janeiro Bum Bum Body Scrub. I looooove that scrub. It smells AMAZING and the smell stays with you. You know how most body scrubs smell nice but as soon as you’re done using it, you can’t really smell it on you? Well, the Bum Bum Body Scrub isn’t like that! You can smell it on you after, heck, my whole apartment smells like coconut after using it! BUUUUT it’s $42 and it’s a sugar scrub so it goes FAST. I also hate the container it comes in. It’s cute, but it’s a pain to open in the shower, get your hand in there and get some scrub out, and it dissolves pretty quick as water hits it since it’s a sugar scrub. So, I wanted a sugar scrub that was more affordable, but still smelled great, that wasn’t such a pain to get out in the shower, and that possibly didn’t dissolve so quick when water hit it. THIS SCRUB CHECKS ALL THOSE BOXES!

It’s way more affordable than the Bum Bum scrub. It comes in a jar, so you have to screw the top off, similar to the Bum Bum scrub. But, a lot easier. It smells amazing, like vanilla. It isn’t as strong smelling as the Bum Bum scrub, but I still feel like I can smell it on me after my shower. The BEST part....this is a “Sugar Balm Body Scrub.” The balm makes it kind of like a thicker, kind of paste. It is easier to pick up with your hands, spread on your body, and it doesn’t dissolve anywhere close to as quick as most sugar scrubs.

Overall, I LOVE this scrub! I will definitely replace it when I run out, and definitely recommend it!

UPDATE - The first few times I used this, I don’t know how I didn’t notice. But, when I was using it again, I saw a loose hair from my head on my arm, I went to pick it up and as I did, my nails kind of scraped against my skin. I felt gunk go under my nails. I looked and saw all this gunk under the 2 nails that scraped against my skin! I was like, “WHAT THE HECK?!” So, then I took my nails and scraped against another area I’d used the scrub at and the same thing happened. I remembered people saying this left a film on their skin, which at the time I initially wrote my review I didn’t feel it did. But, now I DEFINITELY say it does. BUT, it can be washed off. After I scraped my skin and found out about the gunk, I took a regular body wash on a wash cloth and went over the areas I’d used the scrub. After that I scraped my nails over the areas again and, thankfully, no gunk. So, you can get the residue off. Now, whether or not you want to go through scrubbing your body with this scrub and then go over it again with soap or body wash, that’s up to you. For me, it’s not a big deal because I like how this is a balm that doesn’t rinse away as quickly as a regular sugar scrub does. I like that I can spread it onto my body and then scrub without worrying about it melting away as soon as it touches my skin. So, I’m okay dealing with having to go over the areas with a body wash after using it. But, I’m definitely going to keep searching to find the perfect body sugar scrub that is affordable and doesn’t melt away quickly like this one, but that doesn’t leave a film I have to wash off after using it. So, I’m dropping my rating down from a 5 to a 3. I thought about only dropping it to a 4 since I still like it and am willing to deal with having to go over and wash again where I used it. But, it is still kind of a pain to have to do, so I decided to drop it to a 3.

review_title: Unless You Have Very Sensitive Skin, These are for You
review_text:
I love my PMD Personal Microdermabrasion Device. I had been using the green discs for moderate abrasion because I didn't want to harm my skin, but, because I don't have sensitive skin, I soon moved up to the very coarse red discs. What a difference they made! I love them, and they didn't irritate my skin at all. (If you're just beginning microdermabrasion, however, I would advise beginning with something delicate or moderate to see how your skin reacts.)

Like some of the other reviewers, I thought the moderate discs were doing a good job, and they were, but the red are vastly superior. They remove many more dead and dull skin cells, and, additionally, I use them on my arms and legs as well. My skin does feel a little sensitive after I use these, and I would greatly advise investing in the cleanser, toner, and recovery cream especially made for use with this device. (Skin is less sensitive than it is after dermaneedling, however.) I usually use this device in the evening, and the next day, i go lighter on my skin care routine, still using the PMD products and of course, sunscreen. Your skin will be more vulnerable after one of these treatments, even if you don't feel any stinging at all. Go easy on any products containing acid, especially glycolic, which can make you far more susceptible to sun damage. I do use a glycolic toner in the morning, and a glycolic resurfacing cream at night, but I wait about two nights after using this device to do so.

This device, and these discs, have really improved my skin. I have no discoloration, no visible pores, no superficial lines or wrinkles. This device has helped me develop the coveted "glass skin" face. My arms have lost the "sun freckles" I developed a few years ago, due to lack of sunscreen (won't make that mistake again) and they, too are very smooth. None of those little bumps some of us can develop. Just arms as smooth as silk.

This is the only home microdermabrasion device I've found that can equal a salon treatment. It's so easy to use, and it's so convenient. It's always ready for me, anytime I want to use it. No scheduling appointments, no drive to the spa, then another drive back home. I can pamper myself right in my own brand new bathroom, which was designed to contain a mini-spa. I love it! I really love the fresh, radiant, glowing skin this device gives me. But, you do have to use it twice a month to keep the glow. Believe me, the few minutes it takes to use this are certainly worth it. (Keep the device moving, don't hold it in one place.)

I use this device twice a month, and will continue to do so. And, I may buy the discs that are made especially for the body to use on my arms and legs. In fact, I know I will.

I've never been disappointed by a PMD device or product yet, and I don't believe I ever will be.

An important aspect, which isn't a cosmetic affect, is the plastic grommet that acts as a bearing between the metal arm/axle and the stone rollers. This plastic piece facilitates a quiet and smooth rolling action; without this grommet, there's a good possibility of noticeable squeaking and a 'rough' rolling motion. review_title: Effective Lotion for Intense Skin Needs
review_text:
There is much to appreciate about this Zeroid Intensive Lotion for Severe Dry & Disordered Skin. This is a Korean-made product and I do tend to be a fan of most Korean skin care products.

This arrives in a 6.76 ounce bottle. It was nicely sealed. I was modestly concerned about the product's clearly labeled manufacturing date 3/11/2020 indicating I'm receiving it over 16 months after the manufacturing date. While this isn't always an issue, it doesn't particularly instill confidence.

This lotion uses what the manufacturer calls MLE Technology along with Defensamide and Ceramides along with Squalane for moisturizing. It is noted as being good for all ages including babies and children.

While I had some concerns, I'm overall pleased with the product's performance. This is a white, smooth lotion that applies easily. I'd actually just had some seasonal allergy reactions on my skin while working in the yard and opted to use this on my skin. It soothed my skin greatly and has gone to work surprisingly rapidly to calm down my inflamed, swollen skin. I'm actually quite impressed.

There's no scent that I can detect.

In terms of value, this is fairly modest. While this is being advertised as somewhat of a premium lotion, I'm not sure I can justify continued use - we'll see how it continues to do and if I notice a definite improvement over other products. However, I definitely can't deny that it's effective and it is definitely making my skin look and feel better.

Zeroid is noted as the #1 Dermacosmetic in Korea for the last decade. It's easy to understand why as this product works incredibly well and surprisingly quickly.

Overall, while I am a bit concerned about the manufacturing date and the price point is a touch high I'll continue to use and compare it to other available products. For now, I'll say I'm impressed and happy with the lotion's performance on my troubled skin.

review_title: Great mask! Helped decrease size of my breakouts and lessen redness!
review_text:
I’ve tried 111skin products before and enjoyed them, so when I saw this mask I was excited to try it.

I get hormonal breakouts on my chin area and around my mouth. I thought by 35 I’d be done having to deal with breakouts, but nope. So, I’m always looking for something that is helpful to my skin and breakouts. When I saw this was a mask for blemish prone skin, I was even more excited to try it!

This has 2 separate parts - top half and bottom half. The top half is meant to help control oil and shine without messing with moisture in the area. The bottom half is meant to combat lower face eruptions and calm skin. That was perfect for me since my breakouts are always around my mouth and on my chin!

I’ve had masks before that came in 2 separate parts, but never that has each part targeting something different. Another thing I thought was unique was that these were packaged separately. It seemed as though they were together in the standard mask packaging. But, they were actually separate packaging but just together, when you can separate the package into 2 separate halves. I thought that was really unique so if you wanted, you could do them at separate times. Of course, the top half has 2 eye holes and the bottom half has 1 mouth hole. So, they aren’t made to be used on whatever half of your face you want. But, it’s nice you can use them at separate times if you wanted. Like, if I’m breaking out on my lower half but don’t feel the need for oil control on the top half, I can just use the bottom mask and save the top mask for when I do want oil control. So, I think that’s nice.

111Skin products are pretty pricey for me, and this mask is no differ. It’s $32 (at the time of writing this review), which, to me, is CRAZY expensive for ONE mask. Even though it comes as 2 halves, it’s still really one mask. So, $32 is a lot in my opinion. But, if it works well enough, I wouldn’t mind splurging on myself once in a while to get it.

I do feel like the mask works well. The top half didn’t dry my skin out at all, but did help with oiliness. The bottom half helped lessen the 2 pimples I had - they decreased in size by the next day and weren’t as red.

Overall, I think this is a really nice mask. The only downside I found is that it’s $32 for a single mask! That’s pricey! It works really well though. So, it will definitely be something I’d be willing to splurge on once in a while to treat myself or if I feel I really need it! If you’re able to spend it or willing to splurge for it, I recommend it!

- The bottle has a rubberized texture, which is nice to hold and won't slip even if your hands are slippery with the oil which is a nice touch

- After washing my face, I applied 1 pump of oil on my by-then very dry face
- It goes on easily but my hands became shiny and oily
- This did not absorb readily and I had to rub in the oil for quite a while until the shine subsided a bit

- For me, it was a bit too heavy - perhaps I'll try mixing this in with another moisturizer and apply it before bed as a sleep mask?

review_text: I have to say, that my experience with Korean skin care products is really fantastic. I do have combination type skin with an oilier T zone, and drier areas that surround my chin. As such, I do find it difficult to find products that walk that fine line between exacerbating the oiliness and solving the dryness, or tamping down the oiliness and exacerbating the dryness. Hydrating products generally don't do too well for my T zone, but I need them for my dryer spots that surround my chin. This recovery cream works extremely well at hydrating the skin, and is a nice texture and consistency that saturates very well and doesn't leave the skin feeling greasy. That is key for me, because I was able to use it on all of my face, and not worry about exacerbating either issue that I have. I found that the finish that it left on my oilier t zone, was surprisingly matte, and not glossy at all. As for the dry areas around my chin, this cream did wonders. At first I thought to use it as a spot treatment cream for myself, using it only on my chin to hydrate the dry skin that I have there, but I was pleasantly surprised to see that I could use it on both my oily skin, and my dry skin. A little of this cream certainly goes a long way, as I only needed about a dime to a nickel sized amount, in order to cover my entire face. The flaking skin issues that I often have on my chin, were completely alleviated. In my experience, this is another hit for Korea's skin care industry. I found the packaging to be rather subdued, but certainly adequate enough considering the price point. That for me is another nice thing, as I found it to be fairly reasonably priced. All in all, my experience with it was tremendous, and so I would recommend it.
